#3644. Xbox’s Recent Efforts Haven’t Changed Anything And The Future Remains Bleak, Expert Says

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has undertaken a number of efforts thus far to help get the business back into a healthy place, and nothing has worked, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella says.

He told The Game Business that based on the sales and engagement data he sees for the US gaming industry, "I'm not seeing [the moves] have any positive impact" for Xbox.

The disc-to-digital program "hasn't changed their sales of new physical software trend at all," he added. Additionally, making Gears of War: E-Day exclusive on console to Xbox "hasn't made any difference" in terms of selling more Xbox hardware. In fact, Xbox sales continue to spiral. Sharma says there is a supply issue, but, in the US at least, you can get a new Xbox very easily.

Piscatella said E-Day is a "Gears-ass Gears of War game," and a gorgeous one. But making it exclusive to Xbox created a scenario where "you chop the legs out" from under its potential potential to boost Xbox generally. "At least in the short term, it hasn't made a difference," he said.

There was clear and obvious evidence that E-Day was planned for PS5, but it was never released on Sony's console. Other industry experts said Microsoft purposefully sent E-Day out to die "for hearts and minds."

Additionally, Piscatella said Sharma's decision to remove new Call of Duty games from Game Pass was another loser of a decision. He said the data he's seeing shows that the Call of Duty franchise "lost a ton of engagement" due to Modern Warfare 4 being stripped out of Game Pass.

"And you got no benefit. It’s really hard to find any signs of positivity or hope on that platform right now," he said.

Piscatella went on to say that the efforts Microsoft is undertaking are for "Twitter likes" from hardcore fans. "But other than that, in terms of actual results, I'm not seeing anything right now," he said.

Sharma's turnaround plan for Xbox was never expected to yield immediate results--she only took the job in February and she inherited numerous foundational problems. In a memo to staff seen by CNBC, Sharma said she's taking a "long-term" view to help turn things around, and that includes pushing every studio to return to growth for players and revenue by the end of the fiscal year ending June 2027. Beyond games, Sharma has established a unit called XP, which will expand Xbox's games across film, TV, consumer products, sponsorships, and live experiences, as well as new initiatives in China.

Also in the memo, Sharma said she will push her teams to help Xbox get back in line with rivals Sony and Nintendo by 2027 in terms of profit margins, and then beat them by mid-2030. For comparison, Xbox currently reports about a 3% internal margin, which compares to 9.9% for PlayStation and 16% for Nintendo, according to CNBC.

A 3% profit margin means that for every $100 that Xbox brings in, it spent $97 to do so and keeps $3. A higher profit margin is better, and that's what Sharma is pushing for.

#3643. The Mamdanis Take Manhattan!

Billionaire Michael Bloomberg attended plenty of museum galas when he was mayor of New York City. Bill de Blasio didn’t—not even the Brooklyn Artists Ball at the Brooklyn Museum, a quick 30-minute walk up Prospect Park West from his beloved neighborhood of Park Slope. Eric Adams couldn’t wait to get his own tickets to art shindigs; in 2022, a few months into his one-and-only term as mayor, he arrived at the Met Gala red carpet wearing a long leather jacket emblazoned with the words “End Gun Violence.”

“I walk around with swagger in my pocket,” Adams told ABC News from the red carpet.

The city’s current head of government, Zohran Mamdani, is perhaps the most culturally literate mayor since Ed Koch. Or maybe ever—he instructed the city to invest over $320 million in the Department of Cultural Affairs, the largest amount in New York history. And he pays attention to the smaller sums too. When the department announced that city-funded grants for artists would double from $5,000 to $10,000, Mamdani filmed a video of himself, brush in hand, behind an easel, trying his best to paint dollar signs à la Warhol.

“Not everyone’s an artist!” he says, flashing that Mamdani grin. “But a lot of New Yorkers are.”

But when would he show up in a tux to one of the primo arts institution fundraisers that dot the social calendar, particularly as the fall season starts humming?

And now he has. Mamdani has officially attended his first art gala as mayor: the Studio Museum Gala, held at The Glasshouse this past Monday evening. Celebrating the museum’s first year in its new building, it raised over $4 million for the institution. While mingling among guests at the cocktail hour, Mamdani, who did indeed put on a tux for the occasion, posed for photos with First Lady Rama Duwaji and luminaries, such as collector Bernard Lumpkin and the artist Rashid Johnson.

The event was honoring longtime board chair Ray McGuire, the Lazard president and mega art collector who’s served as chair of the Studio Museum’s board for 23 years—and, in case you forgot, ran his own quixotic campaign for mayor in 2021. Through all the toasts, Mayor Mamdani and the first lady sat next to Studio Museum director Thelma Golden.

Mamdani has a bit of a history with the Studio Museum—it’s where he spent his most recent birthday, checking out work by Taylor Simmons, the Atlanta native currently in the museum’s residency program.

Rama Duwaji, Thelma Golden, Zohran Mamdani, Kathryn Chenault, Rashid Johnson, and Lake Bell

As it turns out, the world’s most famous mayor has had a hell of a week museum-going. On Monday, he also released a video filmed at The Met—it featured Mamdani standing in the Rockefeller Wing and wandering through the Great Hall. In it, he informs us that The Met is not just a place to check out pre-Columbian masterworks: It’s also a place to cast your vote.

“Only in New York City can you vote in places like the Metropolitan Museum of Art,” he says.

The Met and the Studio Museum are both part of the Cultural Institutions Group, a subset of New York cultural mainstays that receive funding from the city. Other institutions on that list include El Museo Del Barrio, the Brooklyn Museum and the Bronx Museum of the Arts. Cherished institutions such as, say, the Whitney Museum of American Art don’t receive city money, though that hasn’t stopped Mamdani from extending his support to them. A few weeks into his mayoralty, he alighted to the Whitney’s Renzo Piano–designed building in the Meatpacking District to announce a few mayoral appointments and a ban on junk fees on hotel bookings. He also gave the museum’s programming a shout-out.

“One of the last times I was here I saw the wonderful exhibition of Alvin Ailey,” he said, referring to “Edges of Ailey,” which was up at the Whitney in late 2024.

Later in the year, Duwaji stopped by one of the museum’s fundraisers, the Whitney Art Party—though the mayor did not attend with her. That evening, January 27, Mamdani instead made a surprise appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.

I’ve been tracking Mamdani’s interest in New York’s gallery scene since at least February 2025, when I was invited to a “Party for Zohran” at the Avenue A music venue Night Club 101. The event was co-hosted by Tribeca gallery Theta and Greene Naftali’s Carol Greene, as well as artists such as Martine Syms, Ser Serpas, and Aria Dean. “The art world is coalescing around a mayoral candidate,” the publicist Kaitlin Phillips, who was brought in to do PR for Mamdani early in his primary campaign, texted me in mid-February 2025, back when his campaign still seemed like a major long shot.

On March 2, I went to the party. After taking in some performances and live podcasts, Mamdani and I stepped outside to chat on Avenue A, talking about the art scene, which he was still getting fully acquainted with. He did, however, understand what it’s like to be an artistically minded person in New York.

“I think for me... Look, I’m the son of a filmmaker. I’m a failed artist myself,” he told me, though I still think the track kinda bangs. “I think that ultimately politics and art, there’s a commonality in the act of storytelling.”

I asked him about his platform for the arts in New York City.

Read True Colors: Inside the global deals and colorful critiques that make the art world go round, with a weekly guide to the must-see openings, auctions, and fairs.

“At the core is a belief that art is something that every New Yorker deserves in their life,” Mamdani said back then. “And that that is not something that can simply be restricted to the museums or a Museum Mile, but it is something that also is committed to the community organizations and neighborhoods in the outer boroughs that are, for many New Yorkers, the only conduit to having that.”

Since taking office, Mamdani has named Diya Vij, an arts-organizations veteran, to lead the Department of Cultural Affairs, and assembled a slew of heavyweights to serve on his Committee on Arts and Culture. He’s also started picking board members for various museums. His campaign deputy Elana Leopold sits on the MoMA board, while Battery Park City CEO Raju Mann sits on the board of MoMA PS1.

As far as we know, though, no word has surfaced on who will be the mayor’s rep on The Met board—the most powerful perch of them all. Adams picked Scott Sartiano as his rep early in his term, and his fellow board members have indicated to me that Sartiano was an active board member who was pivotal and energizing for the team. (I wrote a whole profile on Sartiano, pegged to the rise of Zero Bond, back in 2024.)

But I’m sure it’ll be a thoughtful pick. Even through his meteoric rise, the mayor’s platform for artists in New York hasn’t really changed since that night we chatted on Avenue A.

“Artists have brought imagination and honesty to every corner of our city—from our sidewalks and subways to our museums, parks, and theaters. For generations, they have come to New York to explore, create, and challenge convention, shaping our city’s identity and drawing people from around the world,” Mayor Mamdani told me in a statement. “My administration is committed to supporting them and ensuring every New Yorker can experience the arts. We doubled city-funded grants for artists for the first time in nearly 20 years, and we’re partnering with organizations like TDF, The Met, and cultural institutions across the city to expand access to free and low-cost Broadway and opera tickets, as well as free admission to more than 20 cultural institutions. Because the arts are essential to who we are as a city, and every New Yorker should have the opportunity to experience them.”

#3642. MLB Free Agent Kike Hernandez Shares Glimpse Into His Life as a Dad

While becoming a World Series champion with the Los Angeles Dodgers was a dream come true, Kiké Hernández’s greatest title is “dad.”

“I’m definitely the fun dad. I can be firm, but I don’t know how necessarily strict I am because I’m not the most strict person in the world,” Kiké, 35, exclusively shared with Us while teaming up with Warner Bros. for a new initiative celebrating the iconic DC Super-Villains. “But I have an amazing support system in my wife [Mariana P. Vicente Hernández].”

He continued, “My wife is amazing. She’s an unbelievable mom, and I couldn’t have picked a better life partner for me. My wife’s got everything covered. That allows me to be myself with my kids and just be the same person and have fun with them.”

After another successful season with the Los Angeles Dodgers — who ultimately lost to the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 National League Championship Series in October — Kiké is now savoring quality time with daughter Penélope, 5, and son Santiago, 8 months, during the off-season.

While Kiké joked that his son is so young that he can only “carry him, rock him and feed him,” it’s a different story with his daughter.

“Going on walks with my daughter is probably one of the most fun things that I can think of. We tend to have pretty fun conversations,” he shared with Us. “I always tell my daughter, ‘Holding your hand is my absolute favorite thing in the world,’ and hopefully she might feel the same way.”

During Halloween weekend, Kiké and Mariana joined their daughter in dressing up as characters from Suicide Squad.

“I’ve dressed up as a Joker in the past for Halloween,” Kiké shared. “My wife has dressed up as my Harley Quinn, so obviously, the Joker is the house favorite. Honestly, my favorite movie of all time is The Dark Knight. I think Christian Bale and Heath Ledger made a pretty iconic movie.”

With another season of baseball complete, Kiké said he’s been able to explore some new shows, like HBO’s Lanterns and HBO Max’s Peacemaker.

He’s also been thinking about the future as he finds himself listed as a free agent. While the utility player has expressed interest in staying with the Dodgers, he’s found himself thinking more and more about his family as he waits to see what team he may land with next.

“It’s starting to become really hard because my daughter is five and she’s about to start kindergarten. In season, home is Arizona, so for the first semester of kindergarten, we did homeschooling, and now she’s going to enter the school next Monday,” he shared with Us. “Decisions are starting to get really hard because you don’t want to take your kid out of school. I have a second kid now. We have dogs, so the traveling can be a lot.”

As he calls Arizona home, Kiké acknowledged that half of MLB’s teams do spring training in his state while the other half head to Florida.

“It could get hard having to leave your house, leave the family behind to do spring training and be two months by yourself over there, and then have to take your family somewhere else,” he said. “Those are all things that get really hard, and things that people don’t really think about as often as they should from an outside perspective, but life gets very real when it comes to baseball season. Luckily, we’re fortunate enough to have a good support system and to make the transition easier.”

HBO’s Harry Potter show is truly becoming one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule. Not only will fans be transported back to The Wizarding World, but we’ve been promised a more accurate adaptation of the J.K. Rowling book series. Oliver and James Phelps, who portrayed Weasley twins Fred and George in the movies, are among those who may be tuning in. With that, the pair give their two cents on one moment they’d like to see in the show that didn’t make it in the films.

Fred and George Weasley had a lot of memorable moments in the movies. From attempting to do magic that went horribly wrong when tampering with the Goblet of Fire to really coming through for Harry when he was locked in the Dursleys’ home, they did quite a bit. While many great Weasley Twins moments from the books made it to the movies, Oliver Phelps -- while being interviewed with his brother by Jonatan Blomberg of Moviezine -- shared one funny moment from the books that he wants in the show, and I hope we get it:

I think one thing I always laughed at was in the second film when they’re de-gnoming the garden. And I just remember reading that and thinking that was hilarious. So that would be quite cool to see as well. Because you see them also — they’re using magical stuff, what they do in the Wizarding World but, also, I suppose in Fred and George’s way of doing it as well. So that would be quite cool to see.

The scene that Oliver Phelps is talking about involves Mrs. Weasley making Fred, George, and Ron spin and throw gnomes over the garden wall as punishment for rescuing Harry from the Dursleys using their dad's car. That would have been funny to see in the movies, and I would've even taken it as a deleted scene. Sadly, that funny moment was never filmed for the flicks, but given the show's producers are aiming for a thorough adaptation, I think there's hope for it to be in the TV show.

Interestingly, another moment Jonatan Blomberg talked about wanting to see in the show was a devastating scene that wasn’t shown in the movies — Fred Weasley's death. In Deathly Hallows - Part 2, fans only see the aftermath, with the Weasleys crying around Fred’s body in the Great Hall. I’ve got to agree with the host because, as sad as that scene was in the books, audiences would truly be able to feel the tragedy from The Battle of Hogwarts if they actually see the character die.

In terms of the upcoming HBO series adaptation, Oliver and James Phelps have spoken about wanting to help the other actors taking over their iconic Harry Potter roles if they needed them. The best advice the Phelps Brothers had to give their successors, Tristan and Gabriel Harland, is to enjoy themselves since they’ll be playing the “fun guys.”

The Phelps Twins have a point, as the Weasley Twins bring so much humor and lightheartedness to the series to, in their words, “diffuse the tension.” This makes me all the more excited about how the Harland Twins will be able to accomplish that in the TV show.

Let’s cross our fingers that we’ll get to see some de-gnoming from the Weasley brothers in Season 2 of Potter, which is currently filming. With each 10-episode season covering each book, there are a lot of possibilities for fans to see both big and small moments not featured in the films!

Be sure to check out the long-awaited Harry Potter TV series when it hits HBO on Christmas Day and becomes streamable with a HBO Max subscription. You can also catch Oliver and James Phelps’ performances in the film series by streaming all eight installments on the previously mentioned platform.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#3640. Xbox Wants To Be More Profitable Than PlayStation And Nintendo By 2030

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has an ambitious goal: not only to make Xbox more lucrative, but to surpass the profit margins of its biggest gaming rivals, Sony and Nintendo.

Speaking to CNBC, Sharma said Microsoft was working to achieve this goal by mid-2030 and had a variety of plans in place, from focusing on more exclusive titles to gaining more ground in the casual games market. "We will build long-term plans for our biggest franchises across film, television, consumer products, sponsorship, live experiences, and form new partnerships globally, including China," Sharma wrote in an Xbox memo, adding that the company will invest heavily in Minecraft and that revenue growth is expected to speed up in the 2028 and 2029 fiscal years.

"By Financial Year 2030, our ambition is to be halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry-leading margins," she wrote.

While Sharma aims to increase Xbox's player and revenue growth in the fiscal year ending June 2027, things don't look too good for the division right now. According to Circana tracking data, US Xbox Series hardware sales fell 27% year-over-year in September 2026--reaching a new all-time September low--and Sharma recently posted online that revenue had declined in the most recent financial quarter. Sharma added that "console sales remain constrained by supply," but she was vague on the specifics. At the same time, Xbox console prices rose again in August, making it more expensive than ever to buy one compared with its original launch price in November 2020.

Xbox has also gone through a brutal "reset" phase ever since Sharma took over, with over 1,600 jobs eliminated and several studios cut from the Xbox portfolio. If Microsoft wants to make Xbox more profitable than Sony and Nintendo, it could face an uphill battle, as Xbox recorded a 10% quarterly revenue decline. By comparison, CNBC reported that Sony reached a 9.9% operating margin from game and network services alone in its latest financial year, while Nintendo was close to 16% in its fiscal year.

Xbox's current strategy seems focused on more than just gaming, as the new XP division was unveiled earlier this month. Dedicated to movies, TV, and live events, it follows several recent multimedia project announcements, including the third season of the Fallout TV series, a Call of Duty movie, a Diablo animated series, and a Minecraft theme park opening in 2027.

Few movie franchises have had the cultural impact of the James Bond movies. Generations grew up watching 007 on the big screen (with the movies currently streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription), and all eyes are on what Denis Villeneuve will do with the developing 26th film. Specifically, who will play James. There are a number of names being tossed around online, and someone recently asked Jack Lowden about taking up the martini and pistol as the beloved MI6 agent.

No Time To Die's tragic ending brought an end to Daniel Craig's Bond movies, opening the door for someone else to take the mantle. Folks have been taking bets on who might play Bond next, and Lowden is just one such choice. In an interview with GQ he was asked about the online discourse, saying:

We'll just have to see who ends up playing that iconic character next, and whether or not it's the Slow Horses star.

The actor, who is now 36 years old, spoke about his age changes the way people perceive him. When asked by the journalist about reaching the era when "You either become a leading man or you don't," Lowden said this:

I count myself lucky, in that I’ve had a relatively gradual build. So I’ve been allowed to develop as a man, as a person, outside the spotlight. It’s funny – you go from being ‘a bright young thing’ to just ‘a thing’.

Luckily that process has opened him up to new roles, and now he's a popular choice online to replace Daniel Craig as 007. Whether or not he actually get passed the baton remains to be seen, but the fact that he's allegedly on the short list is a testament to his talent and starpower.

As a reminder, Oldman's comments about Lowden came from an appearance on Global TV’s The Morning Show . He gushed about his Slow Horses co-star possibly getting the role saying:

It’s been rumored that [Jack] is on the shortlist. We’re going to find out pretty soon, aren’t we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack.

While we wait for Bond 26 casting news, folks can watch Slow Horses on Apple TV as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if Oldman gets his wish and his co-star gets to land the career-changing role.

#3637. This 'Nothing' Fitness Smartwatch Is on Sale for $59

If you haven't heard of the upstart tech brand Nothing, it's a UK-based company that aims to make products like cellphones and headphones with innovative features and designs—but at a lower price point than tech giants like Apple and Samsung. Last summer, the company released its newest smartwatch, the CMF Watch 3 Pro, which incorporates AI features powered by ChatGPT, and you can currently pick it up at a major discount.

Originally $99, you can get the CMF Watch 3 Pro for $59 at Amazon. This is the lowest price this smartwatch has been, according to price-tracking tools.

According to Nothing, the CMF Watch 3 Pro is designed for "everyday users and casual fitness explorers." It quickly earned a reputation as one of the best budget smartwatch/fitness trackers of 2025. If you have a Nothing phone, the most noteworthy feature is its direct ChatGPT integration: You can use voice prompts to ask the chatbot questions or set reminders, among other things. Another neat feature, regardless of whether you have a Nothing phone or not, is its ability to record voices and auto-transcribe conversations or notes with the Nothing X app, which is great for work meetings or class.

If you've used the CMF Watch 2 Pro, you'll already be familiar with the design, which hasn't changed much. It still has a round display with a rotating crown on the top right, though the display is a bit bigger—1.43 inches compared to the Watch 2 Pro's 1.32 inches. Nothing has also kept the auto brightness adjustment, which is determined by a built-in sensor, and dual-band GPS support with access to five satellite systems, providing greater accuracy when tracking your outdoor activities.

The real upgrades come mainly from the software: The Watch 3 Pro has over 130 sport modes, compared to 120 on the older model. There's also AI tracking with personalized workout recommendations in real time. The battery now lasts 13 days on a single charge, which is two days longer than before. It's certainly in the running for the best sub-$100 fitness watch you can buy right now.

#3636. WoW: Forever Controller Support Is A First Step To Playing The MMO On “Whatever You Want”

World of Warcraft: Forever will launch with full controller support, a first for the various versions of Blizzard's longrunning PC-exclusive MMORPG. According to Blizzard, the option to play on controller is the "first leg of a journey" to make WoW playable "on whatever you want." 

Speaking to GamesRadar, WoW executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale said Blizzard's goal is to eventually have WoW playable "wherever you want, and, at some point, on whatever you want."

The first step on that road, however, is ensuring controller support works really well. Blizzard is using the launch of Forever on November 4, the latest version of its MMO that reimagines the game's classic world and gameplay with new content and features, as a starting point.

"Looking at where things are going when we hear about Project Helix [the codename for Xbox's next console], et cetera, I think platforms will be a bit more ubiquitous," Longdale said. 

She continued: "I think just doing some of the work we're doing on gamepad [support] is going to give players a lot of flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles."

Having gone hands-on with Forever's controller support during BlizzCon 2026, I can say it works surprisingly well for a game that has been played almost exclusively with mouse and keyboard for 22 years. While modern WoW has added some barebones controller options in recent years, Forever's implementation is far superior, working seamlessly without the need for player-made addons like ConsolePort to make it usable. 

You have a surprisingly number of keybinds available at your fingertips (28, to be exact), making combat and interacting with quest NPCs a breeze. Inventory management and navigating menus is a little more cumbersome, but it does feel like a decent tradeoff for being able to play on a controller or a handheld, like the Xbox ROG Ally X. 

When WoW might be playable on something other than a PC remains to be seen, though Blizzard has made clear that if it were making a console version, it wouldn't exactly be a secret. 

But that doesn't mean WoW on consoles is still years away. Xbox's next console, Project Helix, is rumored to be a hybrid device capable of playing console and PC games, meaning WoW would likely be playable on it. According to a recent report, Project Helix is aiming for a 2028 release, may include a handheld component, and could possibly cost between $1,200 and $1,800 if Microsoft doesn't subsidize it.

In the meantime, Blizzard is plenty busy getting ready for Forever's launch, including reworking racial abilities and making improvements to the game's divisive layering system. If you bought the MMO's new optional playable race, the Skyborne, you can technically make your WoW: Forever character right now ahead of launch day. WoW: Forever launches November 4.

Days of our Lives is streaming weekdays on Peacock.

#3634. Drake’s Stylist Juliet Charlotte Has Seen All Your Memes

Stylist Sessions is a series of conversations in which Vanity Fair’s style correspondent, José Criales-Unzueta, unpacks the details, strategies, and Easter eggs on red carpets with the leading stylists. Up next, Juliet Charlotte tells VF about dressing Drake and, yes, reading all your comments about his looks

If you have access to the internet, it’s likely that you’ve seen what Drake wore to celebrate his 40th birthday last weekend in New York City. The rapper opted for a pair of red Versace leather pants and a cheetah jacket, a customized Chrome Hearts jeans and a suede vest, and an archival Chanel scarf paired with gray sweats. But it was an Hermès by Martin Margiela fringed shawl from 1997—a bonafide fashion vintage holy grail—that launched a thousand memes. Drake stepped out, and the jokes poured in: he was dubbed “pumpkin spice papi,” a nod to his nickname and Instagram handle @champagnepapi, described as a Real Housewife on a girls trip to Aspen, and as someone ready for “Christian girl autumn,” another viral trend.

Drake has been the punchline in culture many times, but—online trolls be damned—he’s been dressing better than ever. Chalk that up to his new-ish stylist, New Jersey native Juliet Charlotte. The 27-year-old started her career working with Ye and his fashion brand, Yeezy, as part of his wider styling team. Now that she’s a year into working with Drake, she’s based in Toronto. She also styles the up-and-coming Canadian singer-songwriter Chxrry, whose debut album U, Me & My Ego was released earlier this year.

Charlotte is a singular kind of stylist, particularly in that she prefers to buy pieces—some new, most archival—to build archives for her clients instead of borrowing clothes that any other celebrity could wear. In her first-ever interview, she tells VF about dressing Drake, and addresses the many memes. Spoiler alert: She’s seen them and remains unfazed—she even found some of them funny.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Juliet Charlotte: I started styling five years ago now. I had just turned 21. Kanye’s team reached out to me, his GM [general manager] at the time, this guy named Laurence Chandler. They were like, “Are you a stylist? Can you come in and do some fittings with us?” I was literally a college student working a retail job, and I was like, Yes, I am a stylist. Of course I can [laughs]. It was around the time of the pandemic, when Ye was at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium and working with Demna. I walked into this room and there’s Demna and all these Balenciaga clothes and Ye. I just wanted to work. I was excited, and I just pretended that I knew what I was doing. I ended up working with him up until maybe two years ago now. I learned a lot from that experience, and then I took on new clients. I worked with [rapper and singer] Molly Santana, and now Chxrry and Drake.

Why do you think they thought you were a stylist?

I was going to school for fashion in New Jersey, and I didn’t actually know which area of fashion I wanted to enter. I just knew that I always loved clothes. When the pandemic happened, all the stores closed, so I had to find a new way to make money. I started to make angel number necklaces, and it just blew up and it was really profitable for me. Looking back, it’s kind of embarrassing, but I was young and it allowed me to buy clothes that I wanted. I would take pictures and post on my Instagram just casually. It wasn’t like I wanted to be an influencer or anything, I just wanted people to see the way I dress. It was a very casual thing, but Yeezy is very reference-based, and I guess I kept showing up on mood boards at that time. So Ye was like, let’s just get this girl in here.

I was part of a bigger team, and Ye would throw me into different roles. So it wasn’t always just styling. Sometimes I was working on e-commerce or doing campaigns, or sometimes it was Bianca [Censori]’s wardrobe. It’s really collaborative at Yeezy. There’s so many talented people that work on everything together.

I was wondering if there was a Ye or Yeezy connection, because I noticed an aesthetic throughline with your personal style. What would you say is your aesthetic, your “thing,” as a stylist?

The Yeezy background definitely helped make me this way, because I want to simplify everything and strip down everything and just be like, let’s just do the absolute best version of whatever you want to do. I’m always trying to declutter. And I really think that came from working with Ye, because he just wants to strip everything back and make it just simple but beautiful and effective.

Drake is a maximalist when it comes to his style, and I appreciate that. I don’t want to just throw my personal style on anybody that I work with. I really want to take what they love and be like, “Okay, let’s do the best version of this.” Working with him, I really just try and keep it in his world and keep it to things that excite him.

Drake out in New York City wearing vintage Hermès by Martin Margiela from 1997.

Hermès by Martin Margiela, fall-winter 1997.

Have you always been into vintage fashion? Or is it something that you’ve developed with Drake to build that into his wardrobe?

Obviously we just had that Hermès by [Martin] Margiela moment, which I really enjoyed and I thought it was fun. But I’m really interested in taking pieces, just random vintage pieces that didn’t get such a moment in the past, because that Hermès piece already had its moment on the runway. It’s fun to bring it back, but the way that I like to shop is finding vintage pieces that didn’t get a moment and reinventing them. Obviously there’s a lot of amazing designers right now, but I’m also not so into over-consumption, and just what we’ve turned into. I’d really rather shop vintage as much as I can.

Drake is someone who has such a wide range of influences and sounds. When you work on looks for him, are you trying to pull from this really wide range of inspirations and aesthetics, or are you trying to be a little more focused? Do you try to speak back to the music or do you just try to be a little more focused on just the look?

Sometimes we’re pulling inspiration from Michael Jackson or Liberace, or another artist. But, for example, we’re in Texas right now. He just bought a ranch in Texas. It’s so beautiful. When I first started working with him and I came to the ranch, I’m like, “You are a ranch owner. You’re not larping this aesthetic. You literally live it.” I was really inspired by the saddle shop that’s nearby and all these different stores because it’s two hours away from Houston. He was already wearing [Western clothing] when I met him. This is just a different variation of it. The Western stuff is heavily in his style now, loves vests. I take what I see in his everyday life and see what we lean on more. Like even this mob boss type of thing—he’s really interested in Italian culture, and I’m Italian, so that influence comes in as well.

He has had such a long and prolific career, and he is often self-referential. Do you ever reference early moments in his career?

We did just pull back in his “FOMO” video. We did a variation of the “Hotline Bling” outfit that he wore. But we really don’t draw back too much, I think because he’s just evolved so much as a person. I’ll still send him some looks and be like, “Oh, you ate this,” [laughs]. I have met him as the person that he is now and I’m like, “Okay, he just turned 40. Let’s just be elevated and grown.”

Chxrry at Paris Fashion Week in September.

Chxrry is building something really strong. What’s it like to work with both an artist that has been working in the industry for so long while also with someone who’s so green?

Chxrry and I have become best friends in the process, so we’re just figuring it out together. We’re the same age. She’s so early in her career that I’m sure she’ll have many evolutions, but for now it’s just about having fun.

With Drake, he just loves clothes and is pretty easygoing, but there’s obviously a lot more pressure that’s involved because he’s so established. It’s very different, but equally as rewarding.

I have to ask about the birthday outfits. I thought they were great, but I’m curious if you planned a birthday weekend wardrobe or if you are more casual about it?

Well, October’s a crazy month, so there’s so much stuff going on so I did a lot of preparation. We knew that we wanted to do a beautiful suit, but we actually had three other suits that fell through before that one. Last minute, our atelier had just made that tux for him, and then I got the brooch, we put on a bow tie. It all came together at the last minute, and that Chanel scarf I had just bought that morning in New York. The Hermès shawl I bought the day before we left for the trip in Canada. Everything is really just down to what he’s feeling like that night. We can do all this preparation, but that night if he’s like, “Actually, I just feel like being more chill or I just want to do this,” we just pivot, and we always figure it out.

Drake wearing gray sweats and a vintage Chanel scarf.

A Chorme Hearts cheetah jacket and Versace red leather pants.

I like that he seems to wear only things he owns, when many celebrities wear borrowed clothing. Do you also do that, or do you prefer to just buy things?

On the record [laughs], I hate pulling. I hate loaning. I hate all of that. It gives me anxiety. I hate if it was my stuff and it was out in the world and you just never know what happens. It could get messed up in travel, and there’s just wear and tear. Things just happen. I know it’s a huge part of styling, but for me, I’d rather just source the pieces myself and have them be a part of our archive and a part of our collection.

With someone like Drake, who is so big, you want there to be an archive of what he’s done and worn, otherwise it’s all lost in brands’ sample closets. I have to ask about the memes. People had so much to say about the Hermès by Margiela. As the stylist, what do you think of that?

I love a joke. I love a joke we can laugh about, but I still love the look. I don’t feel less than or like, “Oh God, it’s a meme.” I still love the look. I think it was amazing. Even when we did “FOMO” and he was wearing that leather jacket with the fur on one side, that was a women’s Saint Laurent piece. I love when men do things that are out of the box, or that isn’t just pants and a shirt. Why not wear a fringed shawl? I was into it, but I could appreciate the joke and I did think some of them were funny.

Pumpkin Spice Papi was really funny. If anything, becoming a meme nowadays adds to the look. It’s already a Halloween costume.

Yes [laughs], I’ve seen that. I was too young, but I always think that if we had the internet the way that we do now, what would people say about Michael Jackson or what would they say about Prince? I’m sure there would be so many memes. There would have to be.

Read Fit Check: Your front row seat to the power players, peacocks, and deep pockets of fashion—and how they influence the rest of the world.

You mentioned the Saint Laurent women’s jacket. Something that I always really liked about Drake’s style is his willingness to just go there and have fun with fashion. There’s something really cool and really refreshing about that.

It’s really just fun and it’s really just down to what we’re both happy with. And as a man, if you’re really comfortable with yourself and comfortable, and you know who you are... He gets so many opinions projected on him all the time and he just doesn’t care. He still chooses what he likes. It doesn’t change his mind. I think it’s just because he’s so confident and comfortable with who he is. It’s really refreshing to work with somebody who’s not like, “Oh no, I can’t wear that. That’s crazy,” or whatever. If anything, he’s just like, “Oh yeah, fuck it. Let’s do it.” He’s really just excited to try new things. And even the fringe shawl, we spoke about it afterwards and he was like, “Yeah, it was sick. I loved it.” There’s nothing that can change his mind.

People may not think I’m the best [stylist] or whatever, but I like it. I don’t trust anyone else’s opinion because you’re not in my shoes, so you can’t really tell me how I should do it. Drake as a person has so much fun with his life. He had a blast for his birthday weekend. He doesn’t care about comments and neither do I. We don’t sit there and read them. We’ll give a chuckle if it’s funny or share a meme, but keep it pushing. We have fun.

#3633. Ubisoft Is Pumping The Brakes On Assassin’s Creed Remakes For Now

What's next for the Assassin's Creed franchise? Following the successful launch of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this--which sold very well--you'd imagine that Ubisoft would be looking to fast-track another remake while it continues work on future titles. That's not the case, as Ubisoft dropped a new update on all things Assassin's Creed, including confirmation that it's not currently working on any remakes.

"One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft wrote. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

While you shouldn't expect another Assassin's Creed remake anytime soon, Ubisoft added that it will still keep "exploring opportunities" to bring older titles back. As for future projects, Ubisoft said that it's making "good progress" on its darker Assassin's Creed experience, Codename Hexe. An update on it will arrive in 2027, and Ubisoft added that the team remains focused on delivering a "unique vision" at the heart of this project. The other in-development title, Codename Invictus, is also taking shape behind the scenes. This will be a multiplayer Assassin's Creed game, and Ubisoft says hundreds of players recently got to go hands-on with an early prototype.

"One piece of feedback came through clearly though: Players saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed. The team spent the past months acting on it, and Invictus is now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions," Ubisoft wrote.

For current games, Black Flag Resynced players can download one final major update. This adds New Game Plus, Nightmare Mode, new rewards, finishers, trinkets, and additional customization options to the Black Flag remake. Assassin's Creed Valhalla players aren't being left out in the cold either, as New Game Plus is being added to the Viking saga on November 5. A heavily requested feature for this particular Assassin's Creed game, the update will also add an optional progression mode where Gear, Runes, and Masteries all contribute to Eivor's overall power ranking. Players can also earn new gear and a Master Assassin outfit inspired by Naoe's look in Assassin's Creed Shadows; a new Mithril resource is being added, and you can upgrade your gear to a new "Divine" level.

While the news is good for Assassin's Creed fans, it comes amid restructuring at Ubisoft that has led to several canceled games, shut-down studios, and layoffs. Trials developer RedLynx is on the chopping block, while 72 people from Ubisoft Singapore--the studio behind Skull & Bones--were recently laid off.

#3631. How A Klingon Convention (& Stephen Colbert) Helped Steve Carell Find His Footing In Hollywood

Join The Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It’s hard to believe now there was a time when Steve Carell was not a veteran in this industry. He really kicked things off with The Daily Show during Jon Stewart’s run and was on a long list of big names who came through The Daily Show in its heyday on Comedy Central. This includes some heavy hitters like John Oliver, Samantha Bee, Hasan Minhaj, Ed Helms, and more. It was Carell though who spoke out about his time on The Daily Show and how some Star Trek fans and Stephen Colbert helped him find his footing on TV.

Apparently, whilst working together it was Colbert who gave Steve Carell some prime (and frankly fascinating) advice. It was in the late nineties that both Hollywood personalities joined Jon Stewart on The Daily Show, but Colbert had a couple of years on Carell when he signed on – though Carell previously said on The Late Show it was also Colbert who got him hired by Comedy Central.

From what the actor told Amy Poehler, he was having a little trouble figuring out how to make the gig work when Colbert gave him the key to opening up the world of news satire.

I know Colbert, Stephen, gave me great advice, which was, ‘Come up with a character, and that will make it that much more palatable.’ My character was someone who didn’t quite understand, didn’t quite get it, but was super serious about everything he was asking.

If you ever saw The Colbert Report, you should know this is the approach Stephen Colbert himself took, but I didn’t realize it was advice he was cultivating in a little petri dish and then decimating out into the Comedy Central world when newbies needed it.

This is where Star Trek comes in. As someone who works with quite a few Trek fans, I’m aware of how passionate and positive they can be, and how much they like to fill up convention Halls at places like San Diego Comic-Con. Apparently, Carell at the time was not. The actor told Amy Poehler on her “Good Hang” podcast that he realized how helpful being able to turn the joke on himself could be during none other than a Star Trek fan convention.

It was while talking to people at a Klingon speakers convention that he realized making fun of these people who were so passionate about the franchise they boldly went where few other fans had gone and learned the language was not the way to move forward. Carell likened the hobby to “woodworking” or “photography” and when he got to the convention he realized The Daily Show shouldn’t be mocking these fans.

I remember doing one field piece which were, it was a Klingon speakers convention. You know, you go and obviously the idea is ‘Let’s make fun of people who meet and learn how to speak Klingon.’ And they were the nicest, gentlest, I really liked these people a lot. … And I thought, ‘No, it has to be about what an idiot I am.’

Steve Carell would later leave The Daily Show to take the lead in The Office. He’s had both a movie and TV career in the decades that followed, and he's among the more recognizable names in Hollywood these days. Regardless, it’s easy to see another path that could have been taken: one where he took the easy route and mocked the Star Trek fans, one where he didn’t create “a character” that later resonated with audiences. One that may never have led the man to bigger and better things. I don’t know if Carell’s ever thanked Stephen Colbert for that little nugget of wisdom, but it was certainly helpful advice.

#3630. Suki Waterhouse Makes Rare Comment About Dating Bradley Cooper: 'Disaster'

Suki Waterhouse reflected on her romance with ex Bradley Cooper in a rare comment while discussing her relationship with fiancé Robert Pattinson.

“It’s quite hard to make something work where you’re both doing these kinds of jobs, when you don’t live in one place and you’re traveling a lot,” Waterhouse, 34, told The Sunday Times of her three-year engagement to Pattinson, 40, in an interview published on Saturday, October 31.

“It is almost a decade [of our relationship] and that is a beautiful thing,” the Daisy Jones & The Six alum continued. “It’s a thing that I go, I can’t believe that I have this in my life and I can’t believe that I’m so happy.”

Waterhouse and Pattinson began dating in 2018, three years after she ended her relationship with Cooper, 51. The singer told the outlet that the longevity of her connection to Pattinson “surprised” her because her previous relationship didn’t last.

“Before I had only ever gone out with someone for two years, and if it was two years, it would have been a disaster at the end,” Waterhouse said, referring to her former relationship with Cooper without naming him. (The exes dated from 2013 to 2015 and made headlines at the time for their 17-year age gap.)

Waterhouse previously opened up about her split from Cooper in a July 2024 interview with British Vogue.

“When something very public happens to you and the story behind it is dark and difficult, and you’re actually not doing well, and you can’t explain yourself to the world, that’s very isolating and disorientating,” she recalled. “It probably has taken a decade to work myself out and actually be able to have this expansion in my life.”

She also said the love she experienced in her 20s was “only ever a fetishization.”

“When you get into your 30s you’re almost instantly afforded a little bit more respect,” Waterhouse continued. “It’s kind of delightful and shocking at the same time.”

However, the Love, Rosie star said she has no regrets.

“I wouldn’t take anything back. All these chaotic ways that my life went, it was always material,” she said, adding that the past “led me to a love that is really pure.”

Waterhouse has kept her romance with Pattinson fairly private. However, she did open up to The Sunday Times about their wedding plans and parenting their daughter, who was born in March 2024.

“It would either be all or nothing,” she said of getting married, noting that their plans to tie the knot are on hold until at least the end of this year. “If we were going to go for it, we’d have a massive party, blow it out.”

Speaking about their daughter, Waterhouse added, “I’m two and a half years into motherhood now, and I feel very confident that we’re great parents and juggling a slightly abnormal life, but I feel good about how we’re doing it and we are both just so connected to her. She’s such a wonderful, happy girl.”

#3629. Artist With Music In GTA 6 Had No Idea About Any Of That

Cliff Richard is among the numerous famous artists who are lending their music to Rockstar's GTA 6, with Richard's classic tune "Devil Woman" appearing in the Netflix Extended Look. Richard, 86, didn't know about any of that, however, or that GTA 6 is a game and not a TV show.

Speaking to The Times (via Dexerto), Richard said of the partnership with Rockstar for GTA 6: "I was told this happened!" He said his nephew's sons told him about it. "They didn't realize I could sing like that," he said.

Richard was eventually made aware of GTA 6, but the singer doesn't know what that is. “The show is a game show, isn’t it, really? One of the biggest on TV?” he asked.

"Devil Woman" was originally released in 1976, so it's now 50 years old. Richard said he's pretty jazzed about the fact that young people will hear his music.

“People will no longer just say, ‘Oh, Cliff Richard is from the past,’” he said. “Because I am, but that past is what makes everything what it is today."

It was reported that Spotify streams of "Devil Woman" surged massively following the Netflix Extended Look in August.

For more on the music of GTA 6, be sure to check out GameSpot's rundown of all the songs in the game. The game's official score by Justice is releasing on December 11, and it will be available to stream and buy on physical media. The same cannot be said for the game itself, which is a digital exclusive. The game will be sold at retailers, but there is no disc: just a code in a box.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the game's file size is gargantuan.

#3628. WoW: Forever Won’t Have Dead Servers

World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said.

In the past, various WoW Classic servers became "dead" over time, as players either stopped playing or transferred to other servers. Those massive drops in population had major ramifications for players left on the server being unable to find groups for raids or dungeons, as well as for the server's economy and auction house. In some extreme cases, Blizzard gave away free character transfers so players could leave their "dead" servers behind.

While Forever is going a different route with what are essentially mega servers tailored around specific rulesets, some players might still have anxiety when it comes to picking a ruleset that will be a healthy place to play long-term. 

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Blizzard said it has tools it can use if a ruleset's population becomes "unsustainable." Senior game designer Josh Greenfield gave the example of Forever's separate RP and (newly added) RP-PvP server rulesets. He said there were initially concerns about splitting up the RP community, fearing that one or both of the rulesets wouldn't be able to stand the test of time. He said Blizzard now believes "it will be fine," but does have options should the worst happen. 

"If someday down the line, if something happens and one or both of those populations can't quite sustain themselves, we have options if we do need to say link up their auction houses or allow them to group for instanced content," Greenfield said.

Greenfield said it's not something Blizzard will jump to unless absolutely necessary and that it's committed to its current separate-ruleset path. Blizzard debated the idea of rulesets during Forever's development and discussed letting players from different rulesets group together for instanced content or combining auction houses.

However, it landed on wanting to maintain distinct communities, in part because of the differences in server economies when it comes to PvE and PvP rulesets, with Greenfield using an example of how it's easier to farm for gold and items on a PvE server. That in turn opened up debates on whether these cross-ruleset players would be able to trade items with one another and the need for other restrictions.

"Ultimately, these are different mindsets, these are different rulesets," Greenfield said the team decided. "Let's keep them separate for now. That is a part of original WoW that we don't want to just throw out completely. But I think the tech is set up in such a way that if we ever did really feel like we needed to make a change, we could do so."

He said those options are merely "levers we can pull if we need to" and that it's important for Blizzard to "stay flexible." That's good news, and will likely give players worried about choosing the wrong ruleset some relief. 

Blizzard is keeping busy in the handful of days left before Forever's launch. It previously detailed how it's making improvements to Forever's divisive layering system in time for release, and announced major changes to racial abilities. 

In a first for WoW, Forever will be fully playable on a controller. WoW executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale recently said Forever's controller support is a step towards WoW being playable "wherever you want" and "on whatever you want."

WoW: Forever arrives November 4. If you want to be ready for launch day, you can technically make up to three WoW: Forever characters right now.
