One of Natalie Portman’s most iconic roles, even twenty years later, is V For Vendetta. How can one forget how great she looked with a shaved head? She just shared her personal takes on what it was like to be without hair for awhile, I didn’t see this recommendation coming from her.

Portman first rocked a buzzcut in 2005 at the premiere of Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith at Cannes Film Festival. It had been freshly shaven on set when she hopped on a plane to go to the glitzy event in between filming. As she recalled about attending the event with the fresh cut in her words:

Everyone was like, ‘Oh wow, she has no hair.’ And then I went back, got on a plane and went back to Berlin and started shooting again on Monday. It was pretty wild to be out in public exposed like a baby bird. I feel like it's something every woman should do at least once in her life. It feels so amazing to have rain on your head for the first time.

Wow, what a glowing review from Natalie Portman about shaving one’s head! While speaking to Harper’s Bazaar, the actress suggested that “every woman” give it a try at some point in their life. She loved it because it felt amazing to feel the rain on her head – which funny enough is the same thing Millie Bobby Brown pointed out about going bald for Stranger Things. Portman had a really positive review for shaving her head, but there is something she didn’t like so much:

I did not love growing it back. I have curly hair, and so when it grows back you just look like a little boy for a very long time.

Another solid point. I guess there’s always a baseball cap for those awkward growing pains? In V for Vendetta, Portman’s character of Evey has her head shaved against her will when she’s captured, imprisoned and tortured in the dystopian thriller. The moment when her head was shaved off had to be captured in one take with three cameras at once. During rehearsals for the scene, Portman said a bunch of men on the crew offered to have their heads shaved in order for it to be tested and ready for Portman.

Portman is one of quite a few actors who’ve left their hair behind for a while for a role. Emma Stone is the most recent example for her film Bugonia, but in her case, she made her director Yorgos Lanthimos do so too “in solidarity”. Though, the pact wasn’t as satisfying as Stone thought it would be. Florence Pugh also shaved her head for We Live In Time, and has talked about how she was worried she might look like “an egg” before officially committing to it, and embracing the haircut wholeheartedly.

You can check out Natalie Portman in V For Vendetta with a Paramount+ subscription. It’s still arguably one of her best movies, so her bold haircut was absolutely worth it.

#3534. Ta-Nehisi Coates on Haley Stevens, Abdul El-Sayed, and the Right’s “Campaign of Hate”

When Michigan congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers yesterday, she offered a curious framing. “I’m choosing country over hate,” Stevens claimed. “This is not anti-Muslim at all.”

Rogers, for his part, invoked Martin Luther King Jr.: “You cannot solve darkness with darkness; you have to solve it with light. You can’t solve hate with hate; you have to solve it with love.” For the site of their hard launch, the odd couple chose Perfecting Church, a Black church in Detroit, evidently seeking to exploit the aura of social justice implicit in the Black faith tradition.

Aura farming aside, it is very hard to square the claims of patriotism and love with the actual campaign that Stevens now supports. Indeed, since the moment Abdul El-Sayed triumphed in the Democratic Senate primary, Rogers has made his views of his opponent clear. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice,” he claimed the morning after El-Sayed won. “Never in a million years did I think that I would be running against someone who believes America deserved 9/11.” (Never mind that Hasan Piker, not El-Sayed, said the 9/11 quote, which El-Sayed has disavowed.)

Indeed, a consistent theme of Rogers’s campaign has been the implication that El-Sayed is a tool for shadowy forces originating in the East. “The Muslim Brotherhood celebrated exactly one victory in the United States in the primary this year,” Rogers claimed. “Abdul El-Sayed’s.” As a factual matter, the attack is highly dubious. But facts are not the point, so much as the deployment of “Muslim” as a slur.

To understand this, one need only look to the overlord of the Rogers campaign, President Donald Trump. As is his wont, Trump delights in mangling El-Sayed’s name, referring to him as “Abduladadalalalala” or simply “Mohamed.” “Somebody said his name isn’t Mohamed,” Trump told attendees at a rally. “I’m the president, I can call him whatever the hell I want. To me, he’s Mohamed.”

The Trump theory of El-Sayed holds that his ascendance is being facilitated by the machinations of Wayne County, a “strictly Third World” jurisdiction that seeks to elevate to Congress a “jihadist” who shouldn’t even be eligible for “a seat on an airplane.” If seated in the world’s greatest deliberative body, El-Sayed, the theory holds, would execute his dastardly plan to ban Christmas and—you guessed it—impose Sharia law.

Trump’s attacks have been echoed and amplified by right-wing news outlets like Newsmax, which has lambasted El-Sayed as an “anti-Israel Muslim,” an “immigrant from another Muslim country,” and a Midwest variant of that other alien, Zohran Mamdani, the “socialist Muslim who’s always smiling.” For those too dense to catch the message, the Newsmax chyrons have helpfully driven home the point—“THE LEFT IS FORGETTING THE HEINOUS ATTACKS OF 9/11,” “DEMOCRATS DROOL OVER NON-WHITE SOCIALISTS,” “MUSLIMS TELL US THEY’RE TAKING OVER, AND THEY ARE.”

Lest one think that this bigotry is merely limited to the crude ramblings of unlettered ogres, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has stepped in to offer some intellectual heft to the attack. The Muslim Brotherhood, according to Kennedy, is responsible for not just the menace that is El-Sayed, but also the dark age that has fallen over the entirety of the Arabdom. “There’s 500 million Arabs in the world,” Kennedy claimed, “and yet they don’t produce science, they don’t win the Nobel Prize, they don’t win the Field[s] prize, they don’t win the Wolf Prize, they don’t produce the literature they used to produce.”

Again, facts aren’t really the point here, and there is no wisdom in debating a quack whose brain has literally been infected by a worm. Nonetheless, it is worth noting the particular history at work. During both his run for president and his time in the White House, Barack Obama endured his share of racist attacks. To Rush Limbaugh, Obama was “Barack the Magic Negro.” To Newt Gingrich, he was America’s “food stamp president.” At the Value Voters Summit, a vendor hawked “Obama Waffles,” a product featuring a racist caricature of the president on the packaging. The tagline was: “Point box toward Mecca for tastier waffles.” That last line deserves particular attention. Indeed, by 2016, the political scientist Philip Klinkner would find that the best way to discern whom a voter would support in the upcoming election was to pose a simple question—“Is Barack Obama a Muslim?”

Stevens, in joining Rogers, has allied herself with this odious culture war, one that is itself tied to a very real war. The campaign of hate, of which El-Sayed is the latest victim, has a simple goal: to render Muslims and Arabs more killable. The latter does not require the former. In 1953 the CIA backed a coup that overthrew a democracy in Iran. In 1965 it supported a coup in Indonesia, the country with the largest Muslim population in the world, that killed between 500,000 and a million people. During the Cold War, the justification for this death toll was the threat of communism; post-9/11, it is racism. In 2008, John McCain confronted a supporter and disputed the claim that Obama was Arab. “No, ma’am,” McCain told his supporter. “He’s a decent family man.” This moment is often referenced as an act of patriotism, and perhaps it was one. But the notion that “decent” people exist in one place, while Arabs exist in another, is the major premise for a syllogism of violent, chauvinist power—wedding parties droned, governments overthrown, schoolgirls bombed, and inconvenient people eliminated.

This long war on the Muslim and Arab world has reached its apogee in the concentration camp of Gaza, where every single bomb was dropped from a plane of American extraction. And the genocide is but the latest chapter in a book authored by Israel, a state whose own basic laws reserve full rights for its “decent” people and something less for everyone else. This is the state that Haley Stevens has claimed to literally see in her dreams. And it is ultimately the defense of this state that drove Stevens into the arms of Mike Rogers. From this perspective, Stevens’s defection isn’t a story about party intrigue. It is a story about Stevens waking up and choosing violence.

#3533. Daniel Craig's Taut 92-minute Thriller Is Blowing Up on Streaming

The 007 star's lesser-known thriller is climbing the HBO Max charts

Daniel Craig has established himself as one of Hollywood's most reliable leading men, particularly when it comes to action movies and suspenseful thrillers. From his gritty breakout role in Layer Cake to the high-stakes mysteries of Knives Out and The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo, Craig has built an impressive filmography outside his best-known role as James Bond.

Craig played the iconic British spy across five films, beginning with Casino Royale in 2006 and concluding with No Time to Die in 2021. Now, with the search for his successor officially underway, movie fans have another reason to revisit the franchise and Craig's career as a whole.

But while audiences wait to find out who will inherit Bond's license to kill, one of Craig's more overlooked thrillers is attracting attention on streaming. The film wasn't exactly a hit with critics when it first arrived, but that hasn't stopped viewers from giving it another look.

Dream House, a 2011 psychological thriller directed by Jim Sheridan, is currently climbing HBO Max's international movie charts, according to FlixPatrol. It's ranked #3 in several countries.

Dream House follows Will Atenton (Daniel Craig), a successful publisher who leaves his job in New York City to move his wife, Libby (Rachel Weisz), and their two daughters to a quiet New England town.

Their fresh start takes a disturbing turn when Will discovers that their new home was previously the scene of a gruesome murder. A mother and her two children were killed inside the house, and the surviving husband was suspected of committing the crime. With the help of Ann Patterson (Naomi Watts), a neighbor who was close to the murdered family, Will begins investigating the tragedy. However, the deeper he digs, the more unsettling the mystery surrounding the house becomes.

Unfortunately, Dream House wasn't particularly well received when it premiered in 2011. The film currently holds a dismal 7% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes, alongside a somewhat more forgiving 36% audience score. Critics largely took issue with its slow pacing and predictable psychological thriller twists.

That's hardly the kind of reception that inspires confidence in a thriller, but more than a decade after its theatrical debut, Dream House is getting another chance to find an audience.

#3532. Marvel's X-Men Movie Casts The Long Walk And Hunger Games Actor As Iceman

Marvel Studios is continuing to build out its roster of mutants. Marvel's "X-Men" movie reboot cast was partly revealed at D23 earlier this year, but there were still some key roles left to be filled. Indeed, the latest actor to join the film's ensemble is Ben Wang, the star of "The Long Walk" and the upcoming "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." He's now set to portray Iceman, aka Bobby Drake, in the forthcoming relaunch.

According to Deadline, Wang is currently circling the role. While he hasn't signed on the dotted line, unless something wild happens, it sounds like he is Marvel and Disney' choice for the role. Marvel's "X-Men" reboot has also found its director in "Thunderbolts*" helmsman Jake Schreier. Plot details remain firmly under wraps, but this movie is clearly a top priority for the next phase of the Marvel Cinematic Universe after "Avengers: Doomsday" and "Avengers: Secret Wars" close the book on the Multiverse Saga.

This particular casting certainly lines up with Marvel's specific plan to make the "X-Men" reboot a box office success. It's no secret that the MCU isn't the surefire money-maker it once was, so the idea is to mostly cast fresh faces and emerging stars here, thereby saving money by not having to pay A-listers. And while "Star Wars" sequel trilogy veteran Adam Driver is on board to play the villain Mister Sinister, he's more of an outlier in this case.

Wang, meanwhile, fits in well with most of the rest of the movie's cast, which is composed of either up-and-comers or actors on the verge of breakout status. That includes Inde Navarrette ("Obsession") as Rogue and Christopher Abbott ("Kraven the Hunter") as Professor X, just as a couple of examples.

This is undoubtedly going to be the most high-profile role in Ben Wang's career to date, but as a star in the rise, it's certainly not the first time he's shouldered the responsibility that comes with a major franchise. After all, he was chosen to lead last year's "Karate Kid: Legends" as Li Fong and had a role in the 2024 "Mean Girls" stage musical movie adaptation.

It certainly doesn't hurt that Wang starred in the emotionally obliterating all-time great Stephen King adaptation "The Long Walk" as well. Some of his other notable credits include the recent comedy "Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass" and the Disney+ TV series "American Born Chinese." He will also be seen in Season 6 of Apple's acclaimed sci-fi series "For All Mankind."

Iceman was created by the legendary duo of Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, first appearing in the pages of "The X-Men" #1 back in 1963. As the name implies, the mutant character can manipulate ice using water in the air around him. Shawn Ashmore previously portrayed the character in the Fox-produced "X-Men" movies, with his final appearance coming in 2014's "Days of Future Past."

The original 2000 "X-Men" was Marvel's most important box office hit ever, as it proved that these superheroes could truly resonate in the mainstream. "Blade" opened the door in 1998, but "X-Men" kicked it wide open. Not counting the "Deadpool" movies or "The New Mutants," though, we haven't had a full team entry in the franchise since 2019's "Dark Phoenix," which was a major bomb. So, the pressure is on for Marvel Studios to get this one right.

The "X-Men" film reboot is currently set to hit theaters on May 5, 2028.

With November here, some people are already making Thanksgiving plans and watching Hallmark Christmas movies. But, I’m personally going to need five business days to mourn the end of spooky season. One of Universal Orlando’s masterminds, Michael Aiello, is totally on my wavelength, as he reflected on making this year’s landmark Halloween Horror Nights happen.

Aiello is the Senior Director of Entertainment Creative Development at Universal Orlando Resort and has over thirty years of experience at the theme park to his name. Since this year was the park’s special 35th anniversary scaring us with Universal’s beloved seasonal festivity, he had a lot to say about bringing it all to life. In his words:

For me, one of the greatest rewards of doing what we do is watching all of you experience the worlds we’ve created. Seeing your excitement, hearing your reactions, and knowing these stories mean as much to you as they do to us is something I’ll never take for granted.

I know HHN has become one of my favorite traditions, and it’s great to hear from the designer that it’s all about our reactions and enjoyment of it. The 2026 edition had a lot of highlights, from the Sinners haunted house, an especially bloody attraction with cannibals and an awesome ode to the Hellraiser franchise. In a post on X, Aiello said creatives like himself only get so many anniversaries in their careers, and doing the one this past season has been really rewarding for himself and his team. He continued:

There’s also something incredibly special about seeing Jack the Clown, Oddfellow and our legendary HHN icons and characters come together to celebrate 35 years of Halloween Horror Nights. These characters represent decades of imagination, artistry, and extraordinary talent, both behind the scenes and in the spotlight. They’ve become so much more than personas in a Halloween event. They’re part of its history, its identity, and the memories of generations of horror fans. Watching audiences embrace them again this year has been an absolute joy.

This year’s event was called Jack & Oddfellow: Chaos & Control. It brought about a crossover between two of HHN’s most popular icons, Jack the Clown and Dr. Oddfellow. Both characters debuted during the tenth Halloween Horror Nights back in 2000. They have become so popular that they’ve made multiple appearances in Orlando. With the season having ended, Aielo took some time to thank everyone involved for basically making it possible.

HHN definitely wouldn’t exist without the many hands and minds that create it every year. Aiello shouted out every division that works on the event including the scareactors and performers "who tirelessly bring the fear night after night”. The Halloween Horror Nights senior director also added this to his message:

I’ve always looked at our anniversary years as a chance to celebrate the stories we’ve told, the characters we’ve created, and the memories we’ve made along the way. Perhaps when the 40th rolls around, we’ll pull that book off the shelf again and discover a few more chapters worth telling. Or perhaps the story takes us somewhere entirely unexpected. That’s part of the magic of what we do. We never really know what the future holds.

The future can indeed be uncertain, but if history is any kind of indicator, the talented creatives at the park will find a way to spook audiences in unexpected ways down the road. Aiello also left fans with this last bit:

As our Infernal Carnival and all horrors within comes to close… Somewhere in the darkness, we direct our focus on the next nightmare… Happy Halloween Horror Nights…Till the fog rolls once again.

Oh, I’m so looking forward to the next nightmare! Before we know it, HHN will be celebrating its 40th anniversary, and we expect even more special surprises. Even though we're heading into the holidays, I feel like I’m already counting down the days for the next scary season!

Warning! Spoilers ahead for the Season 3 premiere of St. Denis Medical, “He Ain’t Noah Wyle." If you haven't tuned in for the NBC show, don't fret as this isn't a huge spoiler, but I will talk about the episode in this story.

St. Denis Medical’s third season finally premiered on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was so entertaining. On top of addressing some of the romantic twists left off in the Season 2 finale, the medical mockumentary continued to bring the comedy. This included some fun references to The Pitt, and I had to ask the creator why the direct mentions happened.

Following Ron’s surgery in the Season 2 finale, Damon Wayans guest starred as his temporary replacement, Dr. Highland. While Highland's a good doctor, it’s not hard to see his mannerisms and the way he dresses are similar to that of Dr. Robby from the Emmy-winning drama The Pitt. Alex even makes it a point to say Dr. Highland has a “big performative” energy and thinks he’s in a medical drama. However, “He ain’t Noah Wyle,” as she says (and as the title of the premiere also notes).

Between the way he acts, dresses, and talks, with one speech pulled directly from The Pitt, it was very clear the episode was not attempting to be subtle. St. Denis has in the past had no trouble spoofing other medical shows. That said, references can be tough, and Eric Ledgin told CinemaBlend why it’s easier to mention some shows, like The Pitt, and harder to mention others:

I always feel most connected to the show when the characters are living in the same world I'm living in. So, that gets a little tricky in the sense that they can't be fans of In Living Color because that would cause some kind of time portal warp that would ruin the show, I suppose. But they can know about The Pitt, you know, and they can comment on it, as that's a popular show; it's in the zeitgeist.

I love it when my favorite shows are name-dropped in my other favorite shows, especially when there’s a clear reference, such as Dr. Highland acting like Wyle’s Dr. Robby. It’s understandable why it can get tricky to bring up other shows, particularly ones that have featured the actors on St. Denis Medical themselves, but this time the whole show reference within a show thing worked.

Meanwhile,The Pitt is only two seasons in, but plenty of healthcare workers have praised the drama for its accuracy. It's also one of the most talked-about shows, and that's another reason why Ledgin felt the need to reference it, telling CinemaBlend:

I feel like there probably aren't many hospitals where people are working there and not talking about The Pitt from time to time. And, you know, as I think Alex says, or at least said it in an early draft of the script, it was like, ‘I watch The Pitt, I love The Pitt. But this ain't The Pitt.’ And so it's nice to be swimming in such different waters from them that we can still be fans of that show and comment on it in a fun way.

Since Ron is back at work following his surgery, Dr. Highland seems to have been dismissed (or at least is out of the picture for now). I'm a little sad to be saying goodbye to the St. Denis Medical version of Dr. Robby already. But here's hoping we still get some other shoutouts to The Pitt from time to time. (Especially since Alex has stated she loves Noah Wyle and would leave her husband for him, so I just know she’s gonna be watching Robby's Season 3 return.)

Meanwhile, fans can look forward to more from Season 3 of St. Denis Medical now that it’s finally here. Aside from fun references to other medical shows, there is a lot to look forward to on the plot front. We've got guest stars coming. We've got more chaos coming. So, stay tuned, as new episodes air on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on NBC, and are streaming the next day with a Peacock subscription.

#3529. A Christmas Horror Movie With A 0% On Rotten Tomatoes Flopped At The Box Office

A new horror comedy film has become both a rare critical disaster and a sizable box office flop. "Christmas at the Kringles" opened over Halloween weekend, though one would be forgiven for not noticing. For starters, Halloween fell on a Saturday which meant most people weren't going to the movies. For another, the weekend's new offerings were a bit lackluster, as evidenced by this newcomer from Briarcliff Entertainment.

"Christmas at the Kringles" opened to just $675,000 on 1,825 screens, giving it a terrible $369 per-screen average and landing it all the way down at number 17 on the charts. The film was directed by Kevin Lewis, the man behind the Nicolas Cage fighting killer animatronics movie "Willy's Wonderland," among others. He's not a terribly high-profile filmmaker, but this isn't going to help his case when it comes to his future.

Perhaps worse than the opening weekend number is the response from critics, as "Christmas at the Kringles" holds a rare 0% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It's not that horror movies need critics on their side. The recent box office success of "Other Mommy" proved that horror is critic proof to some degree, but this is next level bad. A film like this was always going to lean on VOD and streaming, but the awful response is likely to turn away quite a few would-be viewers.

"Christmas at the Kringles" follows the Seversons as they start fresh in a quiet suburban neighborhood where their neighbors, the Kringles, celebrate Christmas year-round. But what begins as charming quickly turns unsettling, as the Seversons' concerns about their son's growing attachment to the family leads to lots of action-packed holiday chaos. The film's cast includes Ron Livingston ("Office Space"), Rachel Bilson ("The O.C."), Thomas Lennon ("Reno 911"), and Donald Faison ("Scrubs"), among others.

"Christmas at the Kringles" was a big creative swing, as Christmas horror comedy films aren't surefire slam dunks. But if this kind of thing works, it can extend well beyond the box office. To be certain, a Christmas flick can make its way into the annual rotation, meaning money indefinitely. But unless this one becomes an unlikely cult favorite, that's probably not going to pan out.

There are plenty of underrated Christmas horror movies out there. Even ones with a more comedic bend, such as "Krampus" or, most famously, "Gremlins," have found success. But this was a big swing and a bigger miss. The timing didn't help, either, as it's just a touch too early for people to get into the X-mas spirit, while movies like "Clayface" offered a better option for horror fans in theaters.

Briarcliff had reason to believe it might work out, too. "Terrifier 3" killed it at the box office in 2024, pulling in $90 million worldwide. Granted, that was after "Terrifier 2" became a surprise sensation. The "Terrifier" movies have also garnered surprising levels of critical praise, despite the hardcore gore on display.

Even last year's "Silent Night, Deadly Night" was a bloody remake with something new to offer. It wasn't a big hit, but it was received reasonably well. The larger point is that the Christmas horror genre is nothing new and has definitely led to success in recent years. On paper, this one could have worked. But in practice, it's a disaster in every way success is generally measured in Hollywood.

"Christmas at the Kringles" is in theaters now.

#3528. My Favorite Travel Headphones Are $250 Off Right Now

As a headphone reviewer, not many headphones outside of the flagship Sony, Bose, and Apple models get me excited. However, the JBL Tour One M3 Smart Tx headphones became the exception to that rule when I started using them over my Sony 1000XM6 as my go-to headphones. And right now, the Tour One M3s are down to $199.95 (originally $449.95), their lowest price ever, according to price-tracking tools. This is a great deal for these headphones, which I deemed my favorite travel headphones in my review.

Everything from design to the features on the Tour One M3 was made with travel in mind. The headphones are very light, which, along with the comfortable soft earcups and headband, makes them great for wearing for long periods of time. I was able to wear these on a long flight without feeling any discomfort. Feeling like you're not wearing any headphones is the gold standard for comfort, and the Tour One M3 nails that aspect. The battery life is also impressive, with up to 70 hours with ANC off and 40 hours with it on.

The travel case is compact, convenient, and has extra storage for the audio transmitter, which is the best feature of the Tour One M3. This is a high-quality, low-latency audio transmitter. Anything that you can plug an AUX cable, USB, or USB-C port into can stream high-quality, 24-bit audio wirelessly to the Tour One M3. The main way most people will use these headphones is by plugging them into the in-flight entertainment, which lets you watch movies in high-quality LDAC with ANC. But I've also been able to use them to watch TV.

The Tour One M3 Smart Tx are incredible traveling headphones, especially at $199.95, and I recommend them to anyone who values comfort, battery life, simplicity, and likes the idea of the audio transmitter.

#3527. 2024's Best Action Game Is (Mostly) Just as Good in Stunning Switch 2 Port

Nintendo's newest hardware now has a great lineup of action games

Shift Up’s Stellar Blade is one of the decade’s great action games, blending together quick-paced sword combat and powerful parries. A sequel is on the way, but before it arrives, Shift Up isn’t done with the first game. It arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 later this week, the latest in a long line of satisfying Switch 2 ports, even if it shares the same issues as most of them.

Stellar Blade was originally a PlayStation 5 console exclusive when it was released in April 2024. It later came to Windows PC in June 2025, and future entries in the series might be multiplatform as well. Stellar Blade follows a soldier named Eve as she stylishly slaughters monsters called Naytibas as she tries to save humanity. She only has a singular melee weapon, her trusty sword, but, like Miyamoto Musashi in Onimusha: Way of the Sword, she can wreak havoc with it. Combos and different weapon skills are continually unlocked throughout the game, ensuring that skirmishes next feel stale. I’ve already played through the whole of Stellar Blade, but didn’t mind revisiting it on Switch 2 as Eve’s swordfighting is just that entertaining.

Eve also has several defensive options at her disposal that open up combat. Each perfect parry rattles my Switch 2 with intensity. Her blink-dodge allows her to zoom behind a foe for a devastating follow-up combo. You’ll need to master the timings on those as Stellar Blade’s enemies and bosses can pack a punch. While not quite on the level of a Soulslike in terms of its difficulty, regular enemies can still give you a hard time on Stellar Blade’s middle difficulty option.

New costumes are continuously acquired throughout, and Bayonetta-inspired outfits arrive alongside the Switch 2 edition this week. Just like the base game’s outfits, most of them are skin-tight, and don’t leave a whole lot to the imagination. The same can’t be said about some of Eve’s other outfits, which are basically lingerie. The great appeal of a Switch 2 is being able to play on the go in handheld mode on a long train ride or maybe in a park. But with how damn pervy the game is, I’m not sure if I’d want to bring it anywhere public. I’ll bide my time on flights by playing Pokémon Pokopia or Mario Kart World for the moment.

You can’t get much out of the game in handheld mode anyway. Like some other AAA releases on Switch 2, you’re looking at maybe three hours of battery life playing Stellar Blade on default settings with near-max brightness. There are a lot of things to love about the Nintendo Switch 2, but its battery life is not one of them.

Stellar Blade does look good in handheld mode, at least. Sure, the graphics won’t be quite as good as on PlayStation 5 and Windows PC, but that’s to be expected at this point. The biggest issue is in characters’ hair, something the Switch 2 struggles with repeatedly. Eve has an outlandishly long ponytail, which barely renders during gameplay. In cutscenes, all characters’ hair is crunchy, like their hairstyles exist in 240p. Everything else — enemy models, environments, cutscenes — look great in handheld.

Put your Switch 2 in docked mode, and that goes away, for the most part. Hair looks better, and overall the graphics are much more comparable to the PS5 and PC versions. Environmental aspects like bushes and rubble will still pop in off in the distance and faraway enemies will jankily stutter around, but those are minor complaints. Stellar Blade looks great during effects-heavy combat, and it runs smooth as well. I haven’t encountered any notable framerate drops, even during an intense boss fight.

All told, Stellar Blade Complete Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 is a great way to experience Shift Up’s action game ahead of the series’ next entry. It might have some graphical blemishes on Nintendo’s comparatively underpowered hardware, but those blemishes don’t quite matter during the moment-to-moment, adrenaline-pumping gameplay that Stellar Blade delivers in spades.

Stellar Blade Complete Edition will be released on Nintendo Switch 2 on Nov. 5.

#3525. God Of War Star Dave Bautista Shows Off Kratos Physique And Beard In Video

After a truly tragic setback for the Prime Video "God of War" series that saw original star Ryan Hurst injured on set, Dave Bautista is set to make his debut as Kratos. It seems the actor is taking his role as seriously as die-hard fans would hope, as a new video reveals Bautista has put on an extra 20 pounds of muscle to play the Spartan warrior-turned-demigod.

Dave Bautista says he's up to 250 pounds after gaining 20 more pounds of muscle to play Kratos in 'GOD OF WAR'. pic.twitter.com/T6dGrqKiAY

— Geek Vibes Nation (@GeekVibesNation) November 1, 2026

The video originated on the actor's Instagram stories on November 1, 2026, and shows him flexing his muscles while sporting a Kratos-like beard and wearing a "God of War" shirt. Text on screen reads "Gained 20lbs for GOW" and "250!", confirming that Bautista has bulked up to 250 pounds ahead of his debut as Kratos. That's a significant gain, especially considering the actor's recent weight changes.

2023's "Knock at the Cabin" proved Bautista is our best wrestler-turned-actor, but it also required him to bulk up to 315 pounds, which he told Chris Van Vliet on the podcast "Insight" was "uncomfortable." "Now, looking back at it I probably overdid it," he added, "I was probably a little too big." After that, Bautitsa noticeably slimmed down. As a former wrestler for the WWE, he weighed 290 pounds, which means he became considerably larger for "Knock at the Cabin." But as the actor told Van Vliet in 2024, he started dropping weight soon after and got down to 240 pounds. "The more I trimmed down the better I felt," he said, "and I also noticed the more I trimmed down, the better I looked on camera."

Now that he's playing Kratos, Bautista has no choice but to bulk back up to believably portray the muscular protagonist, whose namesake in Greek mythology is the divine personification of strength.

In late June 2026, former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst tore his bicep on the "God of War" set. With the actor facing months of recovery time, Prime Video was forced to recast the lead role, and Dave Bautista was quickly drafted in. Given his physicality and well-established acting chops, he was the perfect replacement.

But with the former wrestler having dropped a considerable amount of weight in recent years, he needed to pack on some more muscle ahead of filming. Bautista began weight training for the role immediately after his casting was made official in August 2026. An Instagram video from early September saw the actor showing off his latest gains alongside a caption that read, "3rd week in to weight training again. 2 more months to get to where I need to be. Like ridin a bike! LFG!"

Now, it seems he's close to where he needs to be for filming to start. At this point, Prime Video has yet to confirm when filming will recommence, but based on Bautista's "2 more months" comment in his video from September, it seems cameras will start rolling this month. That means the 250-pound Bautista we see in his latest Instagram Stories post is roughly how he'll look in the show, which will need to reshoot all the scenes featuring Hurst before it forges ahead with new episodes.

#3524. Phantom Blade Zero: How to Defeat Jing Ye, The Outlaw

Wuxia action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero offers numerous combat options and approaches, but its early hours restrict you based on your available gear. Mounted on his trusty horse and wielding one of the most useful weapons found in the early game, Jing Ye The Outlaw serves as a frustrating Crimson Forest hurdle, but don't lose hope.

There are some useful strategies to get through this feisty boss fight, techniques which will also come in handy later on in Phantom Blade Zero. While Soul's gear is somewhat limited by this point, the Jing Ye fight is an excellent showcase for your Phantom Edge Dread Axe, and a perfect opportunity to practice some tricky parries as well.

The first phase of the Jing Ye fight can definitely be frustrating, forcing you to chase him down while he dashes around the arena on horseback. Jing Ye's naginata has plenty of reach, and he’ll often rush you for a few hits before escaping to prep a long-distance attack. The severed head he keeps at his waist can unleash a cycle of homing blood projectiles, but he'll just as often toss a spinning boomerang blade to mix things up further.

Unless you rush Jing Ye immediately at the start of the fight, he’ll typically begin with either of these projectile attacks, so be prepared to parry. The blade is quick, but the homing projectiles are quite slow and can come in multiple waves; I’ve seen up to four waves fired at once, but he’ll usually release two or three. Parrying the blood projectiles is possible, but expect Jing Ye to rush forward for an attack before they’ve completed their cycle, which can be a clumsy mixup to account for.

Your best bet is to stay close to him, looking out for his blue and red strikes. Note that, unlike some later bosses, Jing Ye’s color-coded attacks do not utilize tricky timing, so get used to immediately parrying blues and dodging reds immediately after those signals appear.

Additionally, you can get a lot of hits off on Jing Ye while he’s mounted and swinging his naginata, and staying on his left side can often keep you out of range of his mounted swings. Use this positioning to chip damage and wear down his Sha-Chi, then punish him while he’s stunned on his horse.

He’ll occasionally do a leap attack as well, especially if you keep your distance. These attacks can be color-coded and counterable, though they’re usually easiest to dodge. You can typically dismount Jing Ye after stunning him twice and punishing the stun, which will chuck him into the dust and begin the next phase of the fight.

For his second phase, Jing Ye draws a spiked shield that can be a real pain to work around. You’ve seen these before in the hands of Maskwalkers in Weeping Creek Valley, but this particular spiked shield has extra durability. Attempt to run Jing Ye down at this point and you’ll quickly ravage your health bar, and well-timed parries alone can't destroy it. This meants that you’ll need to bring out your Dread Axe.

Like other Phantom Edges, the Dread Axe has limited uses—you should have three max at this point—which means that each swing needs to count. It can be hard to find a perfect opening during this phase, as there’s no effective way to stun Jing Ye outright, so expect to tank a little bit of damage while you prepare.

The Dread Axe can be charged into a combo to extend its damage and guard break potential. Simply pressing right trigger will swing the axe once, but your best bet is to charge the Dread Axe completely and trigger its slow three-hit combo. Two of these combos should be sufficient to shatter that spiked shield.

Bear in mind, however, that every hit on that shield procs damage. Using your Sha-Chi Essence ability even once in this fight can outright kill you if Jing Ye’s shield is still in play, and the Dread Axe results in some damage as well. In this case, the tradeoff juice from a fully charged Dread Axe combo is worth the squeeze.

Note that following through with additional Dread Axe swings will not damage Jing Ye’s shield if his back is to you or he’s knocked to the floor. Make sure that you’re hitting his shield with the axe, or you’ll have wasted one of its precious swing.

You’ll notice a few different maneuvers after Jing Ye is knocked off his horse, though these can be interruptible once that shield is destroyed. For one, He likes to slash dust into your face and disable your target-lock. This isn’t a big deal, just prepare to perfect-parry or dodge the resultant strike, as he’ll take this opportunity to leap from across the arena to try and catch you unaware.

In addition, Jing Ye will use an attack you may have seen a few times before, a quick hit which briefly darkens the screen. Attempt to block or parry this attack and you’ll lose all or most of your Sha-Chi, which can then stun you completely. Just to cover your bases, you may want to lean more towards dodging rather than perfect-parrying to avoid this stun outright.

Otherwise, Jing Ye loves to take this opportunity to drain your health with an unblockable attack and extend the fight. If his shield is already destroyed, just be patient and accept that a few of these drain-attacks might occur before the duel is done; just punish him when you can and close the distance often.

The good news, though? After you defeat Jing Ye, you’ll obtain his Outlaw Warblade and its health-draining potential. While its DPS ceiling is lower than Phantom Blade Zero’s other primary weapons, it’s a great asset that can carry you well past the mid-game, especially if you regularly take damage during boss fights and need a top-off. Just don’t use it on any puppets.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#3522. Avengers: Doomsday Ticket Presales Top Supergirl's Worldwide Box Office Run

Superhero movies have been experiencing troubled times of late. But "Avengers: Doomsday" might just be able to save the flailing genre. Thus far, the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe team-up movie has already set box office records with pre-sales, and now, it's just passed another significant milestone. According to a Forbes report from October 31, 2026, "Doomsday" took $125 million in pre-sales by the end of October across all cinema formats. This means that, by now, it has passed the entire box office gross for DC Studios' "Supergirl."

For the most part, DC Studios co-heads James Gunn and Peter Safran have gotten off to a decent start with their DC Universe. The fledgling franchise has delivered such hits as the charming crowd-pleaser "Superman" and the HBO series "Lanterns," proving this latest cinematic enterprise can deliver everything from lighthearted superhero shenanigans to gritty comic book crime dramas. But there has been one glaring misstep thus far: "Supergirl."

Though the movie itself isn't actually all that bad (/Film's review noted that Milly Alcock shines as the self-destructive savior of the DCU in "Supergirl), its box office returns were less than heroic. Indeed, "Supergirl" took in just $126.5 million against a $170-186 million budget, which means "Doomsday" has now matched the film's entire gross before it's even hit theaters.

To be fair, that's more embarrassing for DC Studios than it is encouraging for Marvel Studios, as "Supergirl" isn't a major event movie featuring beloved characters that have been at the forefront of pop culture for the last 20 years. But while a movie that includes everything the MCU has to offer beating "Supergirl" at the box office in pre-sales alone isn't quite as big an accomplishment as it may seem, it's also a reminder that DC can't afford another "Supergirl"-level flop anytime soon.

Back in September 2026, "Avengers: Doomsday" set a major box office record for Marvel when it surpassed $50 million in pre-sales 100 days ahead of its release on December 18, 2026. That was good news for Marvel Studios and fans of the franchise, which has been conspicuously struggling in recent years as mass audiences tire of the interconnected superhero narratives being told by studio head Kevin Feige and his collaborators. As Forbes pointed out, however, "Doomsday" is far from a sure bet for the company.

According to the outlet, pre-sales are almost certainly coming from die-hard fans who want to secure their chance to see the movie as soon as it drops. But 2025's "The Fantastic Four: First Steps" also saw a solid turnout from die-hards before its box office took a hit. That said, it seems unlikely "Doomsday" will suffer a similar fate. Not only is this an Avengers movie, which carries a certain amount of prestige and recognition, Marvel Studios has packed this thing with fan-favorite characters a là 2024's "Deadpool & Wolverine" — which, as it happens, was a major box office success.

With Robert Downey Jr. set to make his MCU return as Victor Von Doom, alongside beloved MCU characters of the past and the 20th Century Fox-era X-Men, it seems likely "Doomsday" will succeed simply by sheer crowd-pleasing power. Meanwhile, there's no getting around the fact that "Supergirl" flopped hard at the box office earlier this year, and DC Studios will want to avoid any similar occurrences with its upcoming slate.

In light of how superhero movies have struggled in recent years, "Supergirl" seemed doomed from the outset. Taking lesser-known characters and turning them into cultural icons worked for Marvel Studios back in the late 2000s and 2010s after 2008's "Iron Man" became the unlikely superhero movie that changed Hollywood forever. But that started yielding diminishing returns by the 2020s, as audiences grew tired of having to keep up with wider developments in the shared universe via middling streaming series and bland, paint-by-numbers movies.

As such, James Gunn's decision to follow up "Superman" with "Supergirl" seemed sort of baffling. We'd seen Milly Alcock's Kryptonian show up briefly in "Superman," but otherwise, this was an unknown iteration of a second-tier DC character who quite clearly had very little box office pull at the time she was given an entire movie. Jason Momoa's Lobo was on-hand to try to increase the appeal, but it was obvious that mass audiences weren't going to turn out. With that in mind, it's not surprising that "Doomsday" has already surpassed the entire box office take of "Supergirl."

Now, the question becomes whether "Doomsday" can, in fact, overcome the issues highlighted by Forbes to establish itself as the true savior of the MCU. The original "Doomsday" teaser trailers were boring, frankly, and RDJ's return as Doctor Doom was met with confusion among fans who remain perplexed as to why the actor is playing a major Marvel villain rather than Tony Stark/Iron Man. But Marvel has clearly managed to increase the hype for this movie since those early days of "Doomsday" promotion. The film matching the box office for "Supergirl" is just the latest sign that things are headed in the right direction.

60 Minutes looked a lot different when it returned to the 2026 TV schedule for its 59th season back in September. That was in great part due to a creative overhaul that took place over the summer and saw several key employees fired from their positions. Since then, a few of those former staffers have spoken out about their oustings and the state of the news magazine under the leadership of CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss. Now, Cecilia Vega is sharing her take and revealing one detail that still bothers her.

Since its season premiere, 60 Minutes has been at the center of various headlines, with a number of those pertaining to low ratings compared to past seasons of the show. On top of that, there have been ongoing claims of editorial interference on Weiss’ part. Vega made such claims in July and alleged that she was pressured to exude what she considered to be bias into her stories. As for her feelings on the show now, Vega said during a talk in Washington D.C. (via The Daily Beast) that she wasn’t pleased:

It pains me. It hurts to watch, from afar. It hurts to talk to my colleagues who are still there. It hurts to see the ratings slump that is happening right now.

Regarding the ratings, it was recently reported that the October 25th broadcast of 60 drew 5.6 million viewers. That marked a notable decrease for the show, which reportedly averaged 9.1 million viewers during Season 58. Weiss recently addressed the concerns during a tech panel and asserted that the show was still doing “tremendously well.” The Free Press founder, who’s denied editorial bias, also said she’d been aiming to block out the backlash against CBS News and her changes on the previously mentioned news program.

The staff firings took place on May 28, 2026, which apparently became known as “Black Thursday” internally. On that day, Vega was fired alongside others like fellow correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi, former 60 Minutes executive producer Tanya Simon and executive editor Draggan Mihailovich. Shortly after, veteran correspondent Scott Pelley was fired as well after accusing Weiss of “murdering” the show. As for Vega, one thing still gives her pause about her exit from the series and the media company as a whole:

I still don’t know why I was fired. I was not given a reason. I was fired without cause. I just find it exceptionally disturbing.

Pelley recalled the staff meeting that was held shortly after his 60 Minutes colleagues and others were fired. The veteran newsman recalled everyone expecting Weiss to be at the meeting but were surprised to find that only series EP Nick Bilton was present. According to Pelley, employees were even more unhappy after Bilton started reading a statement from his phone without looking up at anyone. Months later, Vega seems to have a lot of respect for Pelley and others who have “held the line” or those who are still trying to at CBS:

I held the line, and Scott held the line, and Sharyn held the line, and I think people are still holding the line over there. But what they are having to go through, or what we had to go through, should never happen in a newsroom.

Questions remain in regard to what lies ahead for 60 Minutes and CBS News as a whole under Bari Weiss’ leadership. Additionally, there are more variables to consider following the merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, which has birthed Skydance. Cecilia Vega, for her part, says she’s unaware of the “endgame” and thinks “it’s a real mystery.”

Behaviour Interactive is under fire following Halloween livestream fail

Some Dead by Daylight players are expressing disappointment with developer Behaviour Interactive — and vowing to uninstall the game — after the studio appeared to show support for divisive streamer TheBurntPeanut.

During TheBurntPeanut's Halloween livestream, a Behaviour Interactive employee gifted the VTuber all available DLC for Dead by Daylight. Given the streamer's controversial nature, fans did not take this lightly. To show how displeased they were with the situation, some players uninstalled the game and requested a refund in protest.

Dead by Daylight is a multiplayer survival game where a player takes on the role of a killer and tries to track down and eliminate survivors. It features an array of well-known characters from all sorts of horror franchises alongside original creations. Thousands of players logged in to play this Halloween weekend, including VTuber TheBurntPeanut. During the stream, he received all of Dead by Daylight's paid expansions in his inbox — a gift from someone at Behaviour Interactive.

TheBurntPeanut is a controversial streamer, so many fans were immediately unhappy to see Behaviour Interactive supporting him. Seeing this, Peanut offered to return the items; the employee responded, "We can take the heat! They are yours to keep." The way that they dismissed fans' reaction only made matters worse.

Players were particularly upset over the fact that many Dead by Daylight content creators have been waiting for a long time to get approved for the Creator Program. All while controversial streamers continue to get accepted and receive support from the developers. This has resulted in Dead by Daylight veterans voicing their disappointment and uninstalling the game.

After quick backlash from the community, the official Dead by Daylight account responded, underlining that the anonymous employee's decision was made without proper approval and that their comments and conduct were not a reflection of Behaviour Interactive's values. The studio apologized for letting down the community and promised to review internal processes to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.

TheBurntPeanut responded to the situation during a Minecraft stream, denying the accusations made against him. The streamer is known for not sticking with games for long, so it is entirely possible that he will not return to Dead by Daylight. Nevertheless, for many, the damage is still done.

#3518. One Of 2026's Best Anime Movies Is Based On The Same Book As A Tom Cruise Sci-Fi Classic

In Doug Liman's 2014 sci-fi action movie "Edge of Tomorrow," Tom Cruise plays William Cage, a cowardly public relations officer drafted to fight in the front line of an alien war. Dying due to exposure to an alien's acidic blood traps Cage in a time loop, and with help from decorated soldier Sergeant Rita Vrataski (Emily Blunt), he has to find a way to break the loop and win the war. The movie did not perform especially well at the box office, grossing $381 million against a $178 million budget, but it earned good reviews and, to this day, fans and the creative team remain hopeful about an eventual "Edge of Tomorrow" sequel.

You might assume the nifty premise of "Edge of Tomorrow" is just an action movie riff on "Groundhog Day," but its real origins are more obscure. The movie adapts a 2004 Japanese light novel, "All You Need Is Kill," written by Hiroshi Sakurazaka with illustrations by Yoshitoshi Abe ("Serial Experiments Lain"). The movie and novel share a basic premise, though the movie moves the setting from Japan to Europe. It also turns the novel's hero, a young Japanese man named Keiji Kiriya, into Cruise's William Cage.

Fitting for a story that's all about its characters caught in a loop, "All You Need Is Kill" has been adapted several times. In 2014, Weekly Young Jump serialized a 17 chapter "All You Need Is Kill" manga written by Ryosuke Takeuchi and drawn by Takeshi Obata, artist of "Death Note." Most recently, Japanese studio Studio 4°C turned the story into a mostly 3D-animated film that opened in theaters this past year. The "All You Need Is Kill" anime does justice to the story while making some of the biggest changes to it yet.

The anime "All You Need Is Kill" retains the title of the novel, unlike "Edge of Tomorrow." ("Edge of Tomorrow" was originally titled "All You Need Is Kill," but was then renamed in 2013 ahead of release. Confusingly, it's also since been labeled as "Live Die Repeat" on home media.)

You might expect that the animated "All You Need Is Kill" is a more faithful adaptation, one that strives to tell the real story after Hollywood distorted it. But that's not quite true. While the animated movie retains the Japanese setting, it flips the story in another way: Rita Vrataski is the protagonist. In the novel and "Edge of Tomorrow," she's a soldier who got caught in a previous loop, escaped it, and walked out a hardened battlefield hero distinguished by her large war axe.

In the animated "All You Need Is Kill," we see her stumbling through loop after loop learning to fight. She's more like the novel's Keiji but with Rita's name, and then Keiji being caught in her same loop is the midpoint twist. The movie's ending also echoes "Edge of Tomorrow." The hero (William/Rita) breaks the loop, defeats the aliens, and arrives back at the beginning of the story (but now free of the loop). They then reunite with their partner (Rita/Keiji) with the hope they'll become close again.

The novel and manga's final twist is that, to escape the loop, one of Rita and Keiji has to die. Rita lets Keiji kill her, and he has to carry her sacrifice through to all his tomorrows. Therein lies the meaning of the title, "All You Need Is Kill."

In "Edge of Tomorrow," the soldiers fight with mechanical exoskeletons with guns directly attached to their forearms, while the alien "Mimics" resemble writhing, glowing masses of black tentacles. The manga has a similar aesthetic; Takeshi Obata draws the soldier's uniforms resembling Spartan armor from "Halo" (a vibe also seen in "Edge of Tomorrow" concept art), while the Mimics are also depicted as pure black orbs with large, toothy mouths.

The aesthetics of "All You Need Is Kill" are much stranger and more alien. Rita's armor more resembles an astronaut or a deep sea diver's suit, complete with a transparent bubble helmet. The limbs of the armor are also lanky and exaggerated, with digitigrade legs. The suit looks like it was designed for wider reach than a human can manage, but it doesn't scream "armored" or "intimidating" like the manga or "Edge of Tomorrow" suits do. The aliens are also even weirder, resembling giant, mobile flowers with bright purple-green color schemes.

In an interview with Animation Magazine, "All You Need Is Kill" director Kenichiro Akimoto explained he wanted to depict something a bit different than the "space marines blasting aliens" look of past iterations:

"I wanted to depict a colorful, vibrant hell. The thinking behind that was that this time loop repeats the cycle of life and death. Rita needs to live repeatedly, beautifully, as she faces this inevitable death. I wanted to send the message that life can be beautiful — that's the reason for the film's hypersaturated color palette."

The palette does indeed clash with past iterations' violence and brutality, resembling a landscape of imagination more than a warzone. But at its heart, "All You Need Is Kill" is a romance, and the movie's look grows out of that.

Season 30 of NBC’s long-running singing competition The Voice, currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, is heating up with the first ever Cut Week. Due to audience demand, the Live Shows are back with six weeks of live competition, but before the singers could get to that next step, coaches Kelly Clarkson, Queen Latifah, Adam Levine and Riley Green had to make the biggest elimination in one week ever in the history of the show.

To get into the specifics, Cut Week saw each coach send two artists straight through to the Live Shows while the remaining five had to sing their hearts out as they battled for the last remaining spot. That’s three singers for each coach going through to the next round, with one additional pick made by America to round out the Top 13. While some coaches agonized over who to fill their final slot with, The Voice newbie Riley Green had the easiest selection of the night.

This latest episode breezed by, as five singers for each team, 20 in total, gave everything they had to their performances in the attempt to win their individual coach over. The thing that surprised me the most about this new twist that was replacing the Knockouts, also known as Adam Levine’s least favorite part of the competition, was that each artist sang on a level where any of them were deserving of being sent through to the Live Shows. I’ve got to say, Cut Week was painful, with more than half of each team getting dropped all at once and having to say goodbye to truly talented competitors.

For me, the most shocking decision was the Maroon 5 frontman choosing to let Brandon Diaz, his steal from Team Queen, slip through his fingertips. While Riley Green didn’t get every single country singer on Season 30 for his team, he came pretty close, often pulling out all the stops to get them to choose him as their coach. From the beginning, 19-year-old Joe Henley has been a stand-out, so it was surprising when he didn’t get one of the automatic spots for the Live Shows. But his rendition of the Keith Whitley song “Don’t Close Your Eyes” was so heartfelt from the first note to the last that he earned the only four coach standing ovation of the night.

While the Marshals guest star said he thought he knew he was going to pick before Joe took the stage, Kelly Clarkson declared that she would be mind blown if he didn’t make it to the finale. It made Green’s decision to put Joe Henley through an absolute no-brainer, because he really could end up winning the season.

After the craziness of Cut Week, what I’m most curious about with next week’s episode is to learn who America will pick out of everyone the coaches eliminated. Clearly, I’m rooting for Brandon, but there wasn’t one bad performance from the 16 remaining singers. On that note, we’ll see how that turns out.

While we already know the competition series will be shaking things up with Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity, we won’t learn who Season 30’s winner will be until December. So, be sure to keep tuning in to NBC on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET until then.

#3516. Idris Elba Almost Played A Different DC Comics Villain In James Gunn's The Suicide Squad

If you're a DC Comics fan, then "The Suicide Squad" casting Idris Elba as Bloodsport and using the character as the leader of the titular team was eyebrow-raising. Bloodsport had no previous association with the Suicide Squad, instead being a minor Superman villain distinguished by using Kryptonite bullets (which gets a brief nod in "The Suicide Squad" as part of Bloodsport's rap sheet).

It makes a lot more sense when you know the behind-the-scenes context. Will Smith, who played Deadshot in 2016's "Suicide Squad," wasn't available to return. So, Elba/Bloodsport took Deadshot's role in the movie. Initial reporting in 2019 even suggested Deadshot had been recast with Elba in "The Suicide Squad." But according to Elba himself, neither he nor director James Gunn wanted to replace Smith or his take on Deadshot. But Bloodsport still functions as essentially a renamed Deadshot. He even has a young daughter, Tyla (Storm Reid), who was clearly meant to be Deadshot's daughter, Zoe Lawton, at some point.

"The Suicide Squad" was made as part of the now-dead DC Extended Universe. With Gunn having since taken over as the co-head of DC Studios and rebooted the franchise via the DC Universe, the movie sits in a limbo of canon. Addressing the issue head-on, DC has now released a one-shot podcast — "The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon?" — featuring Gunn plus actors Jennifer Holland and Steve Agee discussing that exact question.

On said podcast, Gunn discussed how he got from Deadshot to Bloodsport. The change was at Elba's request, with Gunn saying Elba may have seen some "negative reaction" to him replacing Smith. Before settling on Bloodsport, though, Gunn considered having Elba play DC's most infamous mercenary character — Slade Wilson/Deathstroke — as the Squad's leader. Indeed, some "The Suicide Squad" concept art shows Deathstroke leading the team.

According to James Gunn, he decided against using Deathstroke in "The Suicide Squad" at the request of his actor friend Joe Manganiello, who had been previously cast as Deathstroke in the DCEU. Manganiello appears briefly as Slade in a post-credits scene for "Justice League," which was meant to set up Deathstroke as the main villain of Ben Affleck's never-made "Batman" movie. Casting Idris Elba as Slade would've certainly precluded Manganiello from playing Deathstroke again. So, as a favor to a buddy, Gunn dropped the idea of using Slade. Thus, with Deadshot and Deathstroke off the table, he eventually settled on using Bloodsport.

"I like Bloodsport so much. I'd like to see the character return," Gunn said on the podcast. "I also like working with Idris. Idris is a good guy, so I would like to see him return as Bloodsport or even somebody else."

That's definitely not a door closing, but it also sounds like DC Studios doesn't have any active plans to reuse Elba's Bloodsport right now. But one character who DC Studios is focusing on? Deathstroke! In 2024, it was reported that the studio was developing a team-up movie featuring Deathstroke and the infamous Batman villain Bane. As of October 2026, it's been reported that the project (titled "Savage Hunters") is a priority for DC Studios.

(Not for nothing, DC Studios is reportedly working on a "Teen Titans" movie as well. If that goes forward, maybe we can finally get Deathstroke in a film based on the comic where his character originated.)

Should we expect Manganiello to appear as Deathstroke opposite Bane? Not likely. Speaking with ComicBook.com in 2024, Manganiello said that Gunn advised him to "let it go," with "it" being the plans Manganiello had for Deathstroke.

DJI may be best known for its drones and camera equipment, but the company has also been expanding into portable power, with the Power 2000 being its most capable standalone power station yet. #3514. 34 Episodes Of Netflix's Longest-Running Sci-Fi Show Deliver A Masterclass In Anthology Storytelling

One of the best shows on Netflix is also the streaming service's longest-running science fiction series, and every one of its 34 episodes is a masterclass in anthology storytelling. Netflix has some great sci-fi shows in its extensive catalog, from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners to Stranger Things. The streamer also has some great anthology shows on offer, like Love, Death, + Robots and Beef.

The absolute best sci-fi anthology on Netflix, however, is also one of the streamer's oldest flagship programs: Black Mirror. While it only has seven seasons to date, Black Mirror began back in 2011, and Netflix has been in charge of the series since 2016. It's even set to go on longer, as Black Mirror season 8 has reportedly started filming. All told, the anthology series has produced 34 episodes, including one short-lived interactive film titled Bandersnatch.

The fact that Black Mirror has survived 15 years and seven seasons is impressive in its own right, but the reason for its longevity is even more noteworthy. Black Mirror is one of the greatest sci-fi anthology shows ever made, second only to The Twilight Zone, and certainly the best of the 21st century. The best episodes of Black Mirror have won Emmy Awards, been called some of the best short films ever made, and more. It's simply a masterclass in anthology storytelling.

Over the years, Black Mirror morphed from a small but acclaimed series on Channel 4 in the United Kingdom into one of the juggernauts of the biggest streaming service on the planet. While it may not earn as much viewership as shows like Wednesday or Squid Game, Black Mirror is Netflix's workhorse. Shows like Stranger Things end after a few seasons, but Black Mirror is still going strong well over a decade after it began.

13 years after its release, one of the bleakest Black Mirror episodes about artificial intelligence is gradually starting to become an eerie reality.

All of that dependability is because Black Mirror is so consistently good. Every season brings at least one standout episode that sets social media buzzing. Even the worst episodes in the show are still good because they all serve the central idea of critiquing technology. A lot of people resonate with those critiques, which in turn makes Black Mirror all the more popular.

Unfortunately, despite its cultural ubiquity and 15-year run, Black Mirror may soon have some struggles with remaining relevant. The central idea of the show, an anthology critiquing technology and modern life, is just as timely as ever before, but Black Mirror is being outpaced. The modern world and technological advancements like generative AI move so much more quickly than Black Mirror, the show can't keep up.

For instance, Black Mirror season 7 came out in April 2025, and season 8 likely won't be here until late 2027 at the earliest. Technologies that seemed speculative back in 2025, like AI that can recreate faces and voices nearly flawlessly, won't be speculative anymore by the time season 8 is here. Black Mirror is supposed to be a warning about the future of technology, yet the future of technology may beat that warning to the punch.

Even the world itself may have moved on from Black Mirror. Back when the show was starting out, it was the only series willing to take punches at the tech industry and tell a cautionary tale about the near future. Now, with the rise of AI, everyone is taking punches and telling cautionary tales. Black Mirror may not have any bite in a world that has already taken its warnings about technology to heart. If it doesn't have any bite, it's hard to imagine how Black Mirror will remain relevant.

#3512. An Unlikely Frasier Episode Earned Death Threats For Daphne Actor Jane Leeves

The "Frasier" revival probably should have been a one-off special, but  we'll always have 11 seasons of classic comfort sitcom hilarity regardless. "Frasier" ran from 1993 to 2004, maintaining a remarkable consistency over the course of 264 episodes. Kelsey Grammer's lovably snooty Dr. Frasier Crane and his family, friends, and co-workers will remain beloved by a generation raised on the NBC sitcom — unless, that is, you're oddly offended by cruelty against rubber eels. Yes, as Daphne Moon actor Jane Leeves reveals in her book "Daphne & Me: My Life on Frasier (And a Bit More)," her character whacking a rubber eel against a countertop earned her death threats from enraged viewers.

"The Innkeepers" is a fondly remembered episode from "Frasier" Season 2 in which the titular psychiatrist and his brother Niles Crane (David Hyde Pierce) decide to take over a failing restaurant and restore it to glory. Of course, nothing goes to plan, and the boys end up enduring an opening night from hell wherein their family and friends are all recruited to help keep the restaurant running as things fall apart in dramatic fashion.

"Frasier" had already ventured into farce with Season 2's "The Matchmaker." But "The Innkeepers" stands as a farcical triumph — despite, as Leeves points out in her book, some viewers believing it strayed too far from the show's otherwise sophisticated humor. But for other fans of the show, it wasn't the shift of comedic styles that was at issue. Instead, it seems Daphne's treatment of an eel in the kitchen of Les Frères Heureux (The Happy Brothers, as Niles and Frasier christen their culinary venture) was a crime worthy of death.

"The Innkeepers" single-handedly makes Season 2 one of the best seasons of "Frasier." In the episode, as a harried evening in Les Frères Heureux becomes even more fraught, Niles Crane — conscripted to chef duty alongside Daphne Moon — tries to bludgeon a tank of eels so as to not have to handle one of the live creatures. Meanwhile, Daphne's patience wears out. "Oh, for heaven's sakes," she exclaims before marching over to the tank, yanking out an eel, and slamming its head on the countertop. She then hands the lifeless fish to a stunned Niles in one of the episode's many moments of broad slapstick humor.

Turns out, it wasn't just Niles who was stunned. In "Daphne and Me," Jane Leeves reveals that she received threatening letters wishing her a torturous death for this transgression. "What I could never have anticipated were the death threats," she writes. "Yep, you heard me. I got death threats for my mistreatment of the clearly rubber eel. As explained in the scene-opening title card, 'No eels were harmed during the making of this episode.'"

Granted, Daphne gave the thing a good whack, and whoever was in charge of providing the rubber eel certainly delivered a fake fish with some convincing heft to it. But as Leeves goes on to point out, her killing the pretend fish was hardly the most egregious example of small screen violence. "At the time, shows like 'NYPD Blue' and many crime procedurals of the present day got away with, or even overtly endorsed, so much unconscionable carnage and brutality," she writes. "I wonder if they ever got letters?" Just in case you doubt the maliciousness of these missives, Leeves goes on to provide an example.

It might sound unbelievable that Jane Leeves received letters wishing her a painful death simply for clocking a rubber eel with a wooden counter. But in her book, the actor actually provides the text of one such letter. "Miss Leeves," it begins. "Every time I see the 'Frasier' episode where you smash the eel's head for a laugh I wish you'd get an agonizing terminal disease. It doesn't matter if the eel is real or fake. It ain't funny. I pray that you get smashed on the head, too." Bearing in mind this was long before the internet age, which means somebody had to sit down, write the letter, find the correct address, then mail it out. Maybe we were doomed before the internet subsumed our lives after all.

Interestingly enough, "The Innkeepers" was a moderately controversial episode of "Frasier" when it first aired. The show itself had debuted to stellar reviews and outstanding ratings. David Hyde Pierce might have felt the "Frasier" pilot was "terrible" at first, but the series premiere earned Emmy wins for Kelsey Grammer, writers David Angell, Peter Casey, and David Lee, and director James Burrows.

"The Innkeepers," however, prompted what Leeves called "mixed reactions." As the actor writes, "Some thought it strayed from the refined, sophisticated humor that was 'Frasier.' I disagree wholeheartedly. In my mind, 'Frasier' was one of the only shows capable of pulling off an ambitious, expertly-written slapstick comedy with such flair and sophistication, adding another tantalizing flavor to the show." Of course, now "The Innkeepers" is recognized for everything Leeves highlights — though whoever wrote her that letter probably never came around to it.

#3511. Nintendo Officially Comments on Zelda Remake's Divisive Graphics

Link, Zelda, and others have a distinct style to them

Nintendo's upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time looks drastically different from the Nintendo 64 original. That's understandable, given the nearly 28 years that have passed since the first 3D Zelda debuted. Beyond the graphical advancements, however, the Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time makes some bold character design choices, some of which have divided longtime Zelda fans.

In a new interview with the developers of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, we finally get, we finally get some explanation of why Nintendo made certain aesthetic choices, including the decision to make Link, Zelda, and others look more like puppets than strictly photorealistic people.

Nintendo developer Aya Shida, who served as art director on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, said that, "When we first considered how to leverage the capabilities of Nintendo Switch 2 to explore new forms of visual expression, a fairly natural direction seemed to be to create a richly detailed world that felt as though it could truly exist. But our goal wasn't simply to make everything look realistic."

Shida noted the contrast between the dark but beautiful setting of Hyrule and the game's colorful, quirky characters in the original game.

"I felt that this contrast was what gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time its mysterious, almost dreamlike charm," Shida explained. "So for this game, we wanted to rebuild Hyrule as a rich, dense world that felt as though it could truly exist, while retaining the feel of the original. At the same time, we wanted its colorful and quirky characters to feel like a natural part of that world. Figuring out how to strike the right balance became one of the main themes of the art development."

Shida revealed that some of the game's art direction was guided by certain keywords: "a puppet-show feel" and "the analog feel of practical effects films." Those phrases refer to creating "a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds."

"We also felt that there was some overlap between these forms of expression and the distinctive nostalgia evoked by the original game," Shida explained. "We began by drawing sketches of Link, Zelda, and the other characters. At the same time, to show the kind of world they would inhabit, we created a 3D model of the Great Deku Tree that looked truly alive, carefully adjusting the lighting and textures. We then presented the concept to Aonuma-san, explaining that we wanted characters like these to blend naturally into a world like this."

Longtime Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma weighed in on that choice, highlighting how nostalgia for the original Ocarina of Time played into the remake's visual style.

"Back when we were developing the game for Nintendo 64, we thought we were making something cutting-edge for the time," Aonuma said. "We weren't trying to create anything nostalgic. But after all these years, the current development team feels a certain sense of nostalgia when they look back at the original. And their efforts to express that nostalgia led them to an analog, puppet-show-like feel. As one of the original developers, that progression made sense to me."

Players will get a chance to immerse themselves in the reimagined Hyrule later this week, when The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time arrives on Nintendo Switch 2.
